Trine was absolutely spectacular. I usually do not enjoy many platformer games, but in this case, I was pleasantly surprised. The visual aspect of the game is just gorgeous. The lighting really does make it feel 'enchanted' (enchanted edition). However, this alone is not what makes this game spectacular. It is the fact that there are so many creative ways in which you can complete puzzles and get about and around in the game that made me stick around. You play as 3 people whose souls are stuck in the Trine. If you play alone, then you have to switch out between the Wizard, the Thief, and the Warrior. Each character has different special abilities, giving you the opporunity to solve the same puzzles in so many different ways. As a gamer, it really makes you feel creative when you solve a difficult puzzle/climb a difficult part of a level in your own unique way. It is all up to you in how you will get around in the game, whether it be using the Thief's grappling hook or the wizard's floating platform (etc). This game is amazing because there are no limits and no standards to how you solve a puzzle/level. It is all up to your imagination :). This is definitely worth playing!

I've never written a review on Steam before, but I've had so much fun with this game I had to say something.

If you're a fan of sandbox games and enjoy exploring, building, and flying around in your own spaceship, give this a try.
The creative mode is great if you just want to build a bunch of stuff without worrying about the resources. Or there is a survival mode if you're looking for a challenge.

I haven't tried any mods yet, but there are plenty out there to customize your experience. Looking forward to giving them a shot after spending some more time with the vanilla game.

This is the most amazing game I've played recently and I have no idea why I didn't hear about it until AFTER the game awards, where it won the best Art Design. It deserves the award and much more.
The first, say, 10-13 minutes of the game is an amazing intro, showing the beautiful atmosphere and also drawing you, and spoiler free but I teared up from what happens. The game has no trouble getting you into it, and the gameplay is also fun AND challenging. I didn't expect such a cute looking, Disney inspired game to challenge me so much (not as hard as Dank Souls tho) and it will challenge you as well, The level designs change throughout the entire game, forcing you to get creative on how you'll pass the level and skills you unlock might feel like things you should have had at the beginning, but that feeling doesn't last and this is really the only con I have for the game, that's how good this is.
Now the story, spoiler free - it's good and delivered very well, and the Disney inspiration is shown in it right off the back, with a very rewarding ending that made me love the game even more. It might not feel original since it IS inspired by others, but it doesn't take away from the experience at all. The Soundtrack is a masterpiece itself, helping you feel even more immersed when playing the game.
Long story short, this game is an incredible piece of art that I would recommend to anyone, even at its full price. This is my favorite platformer I've ever played, and I hope the developers behind this make even more creations in the future.

If you go into this game with 0 expectations then you may actually enjoy this game.
I think most if not all negative reviews are based on what this game DOESN'T deliver (due, in part to the hype created before release) which I do understand because gamers were blatantly lied to.
However, if you approach this game without actually knowing what the developers promised then you will enjoy it.
Its a GOOD game, If not a little repetetive, ( but then what survival game isn't? ) gather this, create that, refuel this, go to point A, gather that, go to another planet, open this, gather that rinse and repeat.
I am only 7 hours in and ive been to a couple of galaxys, maybe explored 7 planets ( not in their entirety ) and i'm beginning to enjoy what's going on. Meeting different races on the space stations, exploring the different worlds and renaming the worlds i've discovered. There's something rather satisfying about discovering undiscovered planets and seeing the differences. ( even if the differences are small ) Different planets have different lifeforms, different toxicity levels (if any) more or less aggressive lifeforms.
However, everything you do is reliant on you constantly mining, as far as i can see there's no getting away from that. To refuel your shuttle you need to mine, to create just about anything requires you to scan your location and go gather the resources you need. I don't mind grinding resources but if you do, then don't bother with No Man's Sky because you have to gather to do anything.
That being said the one major issue I have with this game is the actual mining itself, It feels like my eyes are being burnt out their sockets, It's so bright and "flashy" everytime I ore some iron or anything it's so unbelievably sore on the eyes and like I said, mining isn't a choice. No matter which filter I use (filters change your surroundings to different colours) It still hurts and there's no "brightness" option as such in the settings. I've never had to stop for breaks during games as much as I have in the last 7 hours.
TL:DR
The game is good (so far) If not a little repetetive, Mining hurts my eyes as it's so unbelievably bright!
Worlds seem slightly different but still feels worthwhile.
Do not buy this game at full price though, I got it on sale for around £15 and it seems about right pricewise, the last time I paid £15 for a game was when I bought Rust and I played 1300 hours, somehow though I seriously doubt No Mans Sky will provide that amount of entertainment.

I was facinated when I first heard about No Man's Sky (NMS). It was a long time ago and other games like Star Citizen was also getting my attention. What facinated me most, was how you could travel from space to planet ground without any loading screens and the awe of exploring space.
This was a long time ago, and when NMS finaly came out, it was not that breathtaking anymore as I had seen other games do well on the same attractive points. I didn't go for NMS then, the awe was gone and it was just another game.
I saw all the crapy reviews and thought to myself, how could so many be this dissapointed?
It is now summersale and I decided to see for my self:
My first impression was how "glossy" it looks. The enviroment looks like something I would hallucinate when high on drugs. The flora is simple, the animals something like what you see in "Spore". Actualy, the game looks like Spore on ground - but the creatures are more simple and ugly.
First part of the game is where you run around try to build your ship, so I did. I took of and went to space... and it was ugly. Same "spore-like" hallucinated ugly nonreal space. Some ships pops up, ugly and simple as hell.
I got my "hyperdrive" and went into "intersolar" hyperspace just to be terrible dissapointed. First of all - there are no solar system - just random planets "hanging around". Second of all, random asteroidbelts pop up everywhere and you travel in hyperspeed right through them. I then tried to understand the progress and mission system, by talking to some nasty aliens aboard a Station with absolutely NO personality. I still don't know what the developers want me to do. So I started traveling around to find something to do.
I then understand how incredible bad this game is.
- All planets have flora and animals - all look the same.
- No solar system means there is no meaning traveling from system to system other than to grind information that you don't need. All solar systems look the same.
- There are no missions or task other than those you make up yourself.
- So there is nothing to do, nothing to see - and the controls and gameplay is something that you'd find in a game from 2003.
- There are no other gamers to meet. (no multiplayer)
This game is just.... SO terrible.
Please - if you want a spacegame - go with the unfinished version of Star Citizen. Even though it is unfinsihed and there is almost nothing to do, Star Citizen is a game that gives you tenfold more to do, gameplay, graphics, multiplayer, missions and progression.
Any other spacegame is better than NMS. Go for Homeworld, Kerbal Space Program, Star Citizen... anything else.

It's great for the old-school fighter. Those of us that grew up on Street Fighter II/CE/Turbo/Alpha, Mortal Kombat 1, 2, and 3, TMNT Tournament Fighters, and pretty much any SNK title. Those of us that also grew up on games like Streets of Rage, Double Dragon, and Final Fight will also find a lot to love.
However, those that grew up on 3D fighters and the current generation of 2D fighters won't be as big of fans of this game. The action is pretty fast-paced, but it's more along the lines of you have to practice with *your* character and get good before you take your game online or set the game to the "nightmare" difficulty.
Graphics - 10/10
I love hand-drawn anything, and fluid animation at 60+fps. Keep in mind that you do have to set the resolution to what your video card or IGP can do; don't expect a GeForce 8600 GTS or an Intel Iris Pro to run the game at 1080p with 3D scrolling turned on, but my Hackintosh running 10.10.4 had no problems with a GTX 760 running this at 1080p.
Audio/Music - 9/10
Sound effects fit and music is pretty well done, but those voices get a little annoying at times.
Controls - 9/10
Tight, the way they should be. It's close to how the SFII games were on SNES and Genesis, where everything reacts immediately.
Replayability - 7/10
I have a feeling that once I beat this, it'll only come out when I'm in a mood to play a fighter and KoF XIII isn't what I want to play.
Overall - 8/10
Not something I'd pay fifteen dollars for, but if you find it in a Humble Bundle or on sale for under ten, it'll be worth it, as long as you're an old-school fighter fan. For those that are new-school fighter fans, I'd read through other reviews to see what others think of the game.

Well, after a 40-hour playthrough (steam doesn't record my playtime because I play through FOSE) and completing all DLC and main story, I am left feeling... Bored and annoyed.
- The combat is terrible. most of the weapons feel all over the place, a 6 damage pistol seems to be more effective than a 30 damage assault rifle, a lever action rifle is more accurate than a sniper rifle, I can't figure out if the guns are affected by some lag or if they are hitscan or projectiles.
- Most weapons and armor break down very quickly, and repairing most of it (especially the good weapons) is a chore because you need to find more of them or pay someone to fix them for you (yet most of them don't even have 20 in repair skill).
- Stealth and explosives feels completely useless, as any explosive besides the fat man seems to leave little more than scratch marks even on common enemies and only 2 silenced guns have been found so far (both with pitiful damage and accuracy)
- I can recall 3 parts of the game that I enjoyed, 2 being a simulation and the 3rd being a great conversation where you tell an outrageous lie about wild Bill's fate.
- I was told about a branching story arch and multiple choices, but so far I've only seen the ability to be a goody 2-shoes, a coward, an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and spoiled brat.
The times where you get a choice in the outcome of a quest, it is usually a simple question of "Do you want to kill all these innocent people or not?" or "Do you really want to waste your ammo and weapon durability on these NPC's?". Blow up megaton or not, rescue the kids from the slavers by killing all of them or doing a couple of fetch quests, do some objectives or try a speech check that you can fail even if you have 10 charisma and 100 in speech because screw you.
OK, rant over (hopefully). The point is, I came into this game not expecting a whole lot and left thinking "ugh, finally done". The combat is a mess, the story and playstyles are barely less linear than your average cod game, the branching story is more like a tiny log and the worst part is that I can't say it was straight up bad, just painfully mediocre at best and really boring at worst.
The game has some really good concepts and ideas and would make for a great story in the form of a book or TV show, but playing through it feels like an ugly reminder of the potential that was completely ignored.
It's not the worst investment of my life, but there are far better games out there. Fallout new vegas does story, characters, roleplaying and combat much better and fallout 4 does combat way better.

This game is a fantastic first entry into the world of Fallout from Bethesda, and if you love being whatever kind of person you'd like to be, I completely recommend this game, but it's best with a few mods, which can be located here:
I'm gonna be givin' you the truth about this game, no matter HOW bad it hurts!
Fallout 3 was my introduction to the entire genre, and while I am a young gamer, I like to believe that this really shaped what type of a gamer, and person that I am in general, even the small things.
Now, I have to agree with a lot of people's complaints, which is that the story is actually quite linear. You aren't given many choices on what you'd like to do in the main campaign, and it will almost always end the same way. But the thing is, you can't judge this game purely on the main story, because it's only a few hours long if you rush a bit.
This is an open world game, and when you finish the campaign you can really burst into the world. Well , you don't even have to finish the campaign, really. There are a lot of different people you can meet in the wasteland, and how you choose to use your time can truly mean the difference for your own experience as your character.
It may fall short of your expectations on occasion, but overall it's a game experience I doubt that you will regret, and that I personally think is WAY better then New Vegas, but that's a story for another time (I'll link that review once I come to it).
I personally love the music in this game, and the other Bethesda entries, and I feel that the radio system adds depth and keeps you immersed in your character. Nothing is too out of whack that you can't roleplay!

Didn't particularly enjoy, because I prefer a bit more of a vibrant area, whereas this was foggy and eery, although this may suit you. You take a ridiculously expensive boat ride to a place where strange plants grow, and creatures lurk, and end up in something deeper than you thought.
It's got more good things than bad, so yes.
After exiting for the evil compound of the Enclave, I discover a crashed ship of some kind. As I go to investigate, I see the rocks and dust around me floating up, and I see my companion drifting away as I float up into the Mothership...
I had a lot of fun with this DLC, and while it may not be the most realistic, it still adds a lot of new weapons and a few interesting characters.
Yes, overall it's a fun experience for something different in the Fallout world, and it's fun to blow up some little green men.
This DLC introduces another side to one of Fallout 3's main factions, the outcasts of The Brotherhood of Steel. They want to get a surplus amount of weapons for reasons you can keep your nose ot of, but the only way to do this is to complete an army simulation for the days of the "big ka-boom". It's an interesting new experience, and it gives you a bit more of an idea about the world before it went to "waste"...

Remember Me is very much a mixed bag. The story, setting and visual quality of the game go a long way to help it stand out from other titles, helping it cement an identity as a promising new IP. Sadly, the game is also held back by an underdeveloped combat system, often frustrating enemies, and one of the most linear beat-em-up experiences of recent memory. Saying this, there is some fun to be had out of Remember Me. Combat can occasionally be fun, especially when trying out new combos and S-Pressens, and boss encounters are particularly memorable and well designed. With all that’s been said, Remember Me just doesn’t live up to its potential. A setting and story this good deserves to be expanded upon in bigger, more ambitious games. Quote from awesomegames.

I find Remember Me has quite a unique plot, with plot twists that you won't really see coming, definately set apart from the others in the market currently. Nilin, the main character, is quite interesting and her monolouges inbetween chapters do give you an insight into her personality.
Graphics wise and visually speaking, it can be quite beautiful at times and alot of detail has been put in. I especially love how your Sensen displays certain things, such as a shop's opening time or a cafe's menu when you go near it, yes not a core part of the gameplay but well executed and thought out and adds to the futuristic feel.
Combat wise, you really have to plan your combos for fight and on occasion pause and rearrange them to suit the situation, for example add more healing Pressens, since you're about to die. It also pays to learn the combos and not click the mouse buttons like a madman, I realised this after my first death early on. The downside is that the combat can be somwhat... floaty I suppose as sometimes I dodge the wrong way or attack an unintended target, which makes me think perhaps a controller was intended for this game, which is annoying for PC and keyboard users as the WASD keys do not do diagonal. The camera can also be annoying at times if you are moving around a lot during a fight.
The enemies have a good variety, in that as you move along, new enemies are introduced. For example Nilin's stun move won't work on certain enemies. Some will hold a shield that you must destroy first, or you have to defeat it's supporters so they become vulnerable. It does pay to check their codex to see what works as trial and error can be somewhat tedious and means you die alot.
It's also a shame that there are not more memory remix events as they are quite intriguing and it is interesting to see how moving one little thing can create an entirely different memory.
Overall it's really the combat that let's this game down due it's issues with the keyboard.
I'd recommed playing it but perhaps get it during a sale at a good reduced price

This game brings nothing spectacularly new to the table. What it does is very much what Tomb Raider 2013 did; Refine existing ideas. Remember Me doesn't do that quite as well as Tomb Raider did, in my opinion, but it's certainly not a title to miss. The story, is good. Cheesy, but good. Graphically, this game is gorgeous. The set pieces are astounding, and the art and camerawork, mix with the music to give a very Scifi Movie vibe. This art direction and music direction are very consistent throughout the entire game.
Speaking of the music, Remember Me features dynamic fight music. Landing a combo successfully on an enemy will cause the music to play louder and more naturally, while getting hit, or losing too much health will cause it to degrade to just the basic beat, or sound like it's "glitching out". This creates a sort of reward for doing well, and when the music starts hitting it's high points, and you're on a roll, it feels amazing. The music is on a whole other level. It's a mix of Classical string and brass with digital beats and Synth effects. It comes off as epic, and distorted but in such a way that it accentuates the story.
And now about the combat... I feel the combat is good. There are a few things that cause me to dislike fighting in the game, but it's mostly just annoying enemy types, or too many enemies attacking at once. If I had to sum up the combat in this game I'd say it's like Batman's but the enemies don't wait, or take turns. For some, this is great, and it seem more realistic, but from a gameplay perspective, I feel it adds unneeded frustration.
You play as Nilin, a Memory Hunter, who's memories, ironically, have been stolen. You wake up in a lab, and someone from your past, named Edge, is trying to help you escape being turned into a human vegetable. The story is dark, and while much of it can be seen from a mile away, I felt there were a few good twists here and there. Some of the acting is a bit cheesy, but I'm usually a fan of cheesy acting, and storylines.
The setting is Neo Paris. Pretty much what would happen if Paris became Taris from Knights of the Old Republic. Grungy under-city, and posh higher society areas create a contrast-heavy universe where it's never hard to tell where you are. Things in the environment feel lived in as well as alive. Beams. shutters, pipes, holographic screens, people, wind. Everything is animated, and feels like it's right where it belongs. The lighting is another thing of note. This is one of the prettier Unreal Engine games of last gen. It seems like the developers, even though fairly new, had a deep understanding of UE.
If you're in the mood for a dark, scifi game with a pretty unique and engaging setting, then I would say this is 100% for you. The developers put a lot of work into this one, and it deserves far more than what it got in sales. It's not perfect, but it's great.
Afterthoughts:
I want another game in the same vein, or even in the same world of Remember Me. Neo Paris is just too cool and the vibes I get from the music are intense. It's the perfect playground for a Deus Ex-style game. ;)

People either not being able to run it or some graphical bug that "ruins" the whole game for that for person, any game that's been out for less than a week is flooded with those kind of negative reviews, some add some more depth, but still you cant knock the game at 1-2 hours just because theres a texture bug and write a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t review because you're a little heated you can't run the game. Pro's:

Preloaded the game a couple hours before launch, did the update, launched and was getting 100fps on mein leben settings(Ultra/Max setttings) with no graphical bugs or issues besides a little clipping with BJs arm when behind some of the covers. I would wholeheartedly recommend this game! It is a great and unique take on things in what I would consider a mostly stale market.
The voices and mental aspect is extremely well done.
The combat, is excellent. I wouldn't call it simple by any means, but it is very cut and dry. Light, heavy, dodge and parry is all you have to work with, but if it ain't broke, don't fix it. Even though its simplistic, it is VERY tight and responsive. For an indy game, this combat feels better than almost any AAA title. I've heard some people liken it to DMC or other "hack n slash"  and it is very much not that. It isn't quite up to Dark Souls level of punishment, but each strike, block, and move has to be carefully thought out, especially against multiple opponents.
I refunded for two reasons, and one of those is actually a compliment.
First, I feel it is a bit of a walking simulator. I understand that this is just how the game works, but I felt just a little more tedious than a walking simulator should have been, for me at least. I don't mind walking, but I repeatedly found myself wandering around, quickly looking for solutions to walking puzzles and running through obstacles just to get myself to the next bit of juicy and amazing combat, or the next compelling bit of story.
The second is the main story mechanic, the voices, I think they nailed this aspect, and you never feel alone, or unwatched. I have actually met/known people with disorders similar (though not as bad) to Senua and their stories of how they describe things are eerily similar. To be plain, they did it too well for me, and I found myself very anxious and uneasy while I was playing, and for a short while afterwards. After playing long enough, I felt off enough that I wanted to stop playing.
To be honest, I think this would make a much better movie than a game. I found myself totally engrossed in Senua's tale, and wanted to know every twist and turn of events that happened to her, but the d@mn thing just unsettles me too much. I don't scare easliy, perhaps it was because this wasn't some fantastical world, but a very possible one inside someones head that was the difference, but this one certainly rustled my Jimmies.

Speaking of dialogue, YOU MUST WEAR HEADPHONES! The sound design and voice acting are top class and bring out every emotion that is presented to a much higher degree. The Bin-aural sound design is chilling and fits perfectly into the character's personality. really the only game that I can think of that has really done this...in an effective way.
All in all, I think that this is definitely a game that is worth experiencing, as i believe the response to this game will spark a new chord in mainstream video games. As such, it is worth it to say that you will have played on of the best.

I really wanted to like this game, I really did.
Positive:
-Small development team, who made a playable (not really enjoyable) game. It's always nice to see little dev teams making games.
-The starting price of $15 doesn't leave a bad taste in your mouth.
-Clever take on Van Helsing, with some cool concepts.
-I was expecting a pure text based game, with no voicework, yet I found the voicework to be better than some AAA games being released these days.
-It's short and doesn't overstay it's welcome.
-Decent replayability
Negative:
-The loading times are awful, they might be the worst loading times I've ever experienced in a game. There's also no loading indicator until 10 seconds prior to the next area loads up. So you're stuck looking at a boring map for 1-2 minutes, wondering if the game crashed.
-This games default settings are ridiculous and slow down the game (newsflash the majority of PC gamers don't have crossfire video cards).
-I found a few work arounds to speed up the load times to about 35-45 seconds but even then this game felt poorly optimized.
-I have a pretty decent rig that can still play Far Cry 3, Skyrim, and Deus EX on high, with my frame rate rarely dropping below 35-45 fps. So why the hell can this game barely stutter by at 5 fps?? I haven't seen a game stutter and drop the framerate this much since my '07 gateway when I played WoW.
-Oddly enough, I did find the frame rate to improve if I turned certain specs up not down (seriously).
-The enviroments are generic, the same old muddy sewers/forest/foggy forest/cave, you've seen a million times in generic RPGs.
-This game takes little to no strategy, I rarely died. When I did die, it was usually do to the screen stuttering and having my character jump across  the scene do to lag or a screen freeze.
-The character models are pretty dull, you fight the same spiders/rats/zombies from every RPG. Although they do have some cool looking revolutionary robot soldiers and Van Helsing himself looks alright, even if he is a walking cliché.
-Also for some reason the audio cuts in and out.
-Gameplay is weird, they try to be so different from Diablo/Torchlight, that they remap certain keys and get rid of others altogether. All I wanted was another hack'n'slash diabloesque RPG, yet this game tries to reinvent the wheel and ends up making a square tire.
Bottomline: This game is only worth picking up if it's part of some Humble Bundle or under $2. The forgettable story, boring graphics, frame rate issues, and loading screens will have you uninstalling this monster in less time then it takes to watch a trailer for that lame Van Helsing movie starring Wolverine.

Mirromoon EP recreates the experience of playing video games WAY back in the day.
In the 80s and early 90s, video games were much more mysterious than they are now.  Games were made on MUCH smaller budgets by companies who were generally far less "professional" than modern studios.  There was never a "tutorial level" in the game itself.  The basic controls were (hopefully) described in the manual that came packaged with the game, and beyond that, you were usually on your own.  There was no internet.
Under these circumstances, just figuring out how a game worked, could actually be part of the challenge of the game. That is the experience that Mirrormoon EP tries to create for the player, and I think it absolutely succeeds. Whether or not you enjoy it, depends on whether or not you enjoy that particular experience.

I've never had to stop for breaks during games as much as I have in the last 7 hours.

So, No Man's Sky. First I have to say that I never preordered the game, neither have I been into the hype train for this game, so this is an opinion of someone who doesn't really care about Sean Murray's lies.
This game really isn't for everyone. Many criticisms seem to be about the game being promised as a large scale multiplayer space exploration game. And I do agree with most of them.
For instance, the planets, while massive feel a bit empty at times with only one alien in an outpost in the middle of nowhere in certain areas. The game also plays like a first person survival game, with the need for resources for everything, including taking off and boosting your ship. Crafting feels a bit meh. Get resource, craft, repeat. Space combat is a bit interesting with you needing to aim where enemies are GOING rather than where they are. Upgrading your Exosuit, Multi Tool and Ships will cost you money, and will cost you a lot, making it a bit of a repetitive grind. Combat is meh.
The base building is pretty good all things considered, and if you just want to build play on Creative Mode, though there are problems with that mode, such as it being too easy on the exploring front.
Freighters are also pretty good, serving as extra storage and adds the ability to own 6 ships at a time.
Creative Mode is too easy. No need for units, no need for resources, no need for everything. I felt I rather play normal mode with a cheat table with certain options activated to play at the right difficulty.
Now for the biggest talking point: Multiplayer. There is none. You can share bases on the workshop, and name creatures, planets and galaxies and claim them as your own for units. That's it.
So why am I recommending No Man's Sky? Because it is a chill game. I really enjoy playing the game, and the lack of multiplayer is a selling point to me because I hate online play. I recommend it if you want a game you can play without any real thinking. The price tag is ♥♥♥♥ing ridiculous for what it is, and Hello Games should bring it down.
So if you weren't hit by the derailed hype train of 2016 (no one learned from the 2015 edition known as Fallout 4) and you want a certain game where you can explore space while in your own zenlike bubble, give it a look. Otherwise, don't bother.
This game taught me a lesson to not pre-order games and just buy them when they come out.

A game that received mixed reviews. Some loved it and others hated it. The concept of remixing memories is probably the best thing about it -- I wish there were more opportunities to do that in the game. Once you get the hang of it it is pretty neat.  Yes, the game is linear but for those looking for a cool experience and a nice cyber-punk setting should pick this game up when on sale and give it a try.  I doubt we will see a sequel which is unfortunate as the series could have a lot of potential.

Neo-Paris. 2084.
Personal memories can now be digitised, bought, sold and traded. The last remnants of privacy and intimacy have been swept away in what appears to be a logical progression of the explosive growth of social networks at the beginning of the 21st century. The citizens themselves have accepted this surveillance society in exchange for the comfort only smart technology can provide. This memory economy gives immense power over society to just a handful of people.
Remember Me™ is a 3rd person action adventure where players take on the role of Nilin, a former elite memory hunter with the ability to break into people’s minds and steal or even alter their memories. The authorities, fearful of her knowledge and capabilities arrested Nilin and wiped her memory clean. After her escape from prison, Nilin sets out on a mission to recover her identity, helped by her last and only friend. This search for her past leads to her being hunted by the very people that created this surveillance society.

Characters like Anya, Fergus, and Wyatt get pushed to the side character development-wise in favor of the new characters. Story is good for the majority of the game, but flounders in near the end. Horton (the southern socialist in the trailer) and his crew don't even show up until near the end and do absolutely nothing for the game story-wise. The entire Louisiana mission could have been cut from the game and you wouldn't have lost anything. His character goes completely under-used. The game is too cutscene heavy in the beginning and has numerous unskippable cutscenes that can be very annoying before you can even start to play the game. Also, the last mission is a joke. There is no final boss fight like The New Order and its anti-climatic as all hell. On top of that, it ends on a really ♥♥♥♥♥♥ cliff hanger. The ending made the game feel very rushed.
I had numerous issues with the port. First the game kept zooming in to 1/4th of the original image if I attempt resolutions higher than 1440p. I experienced a few crashes and even a bluescreen playing this game (blue screen was definitely caused by the game). Also, the worst experience was when the main menu glitched out and wouldn't let me continue, the progress to fix my save was annoying as hell and really hampered my experience.
Overall, its a good game but doesn't match up to the The New Order. Also, while it performs very well, there are still numerous issues not unlike the first game. Might want to wait until they patch some of the issues. Last thing, the game is much more political than the first one so if you're the type of person who thinks stuff like white genocide is real, then you're not going to like this game.

The Incredible Adventures of Van Helsing represents a solid action role-playing game, based on Bram Stoker’s legendary vampire slayer. It has a charming atmosphere in combination with an interesting storyline and lovely characters, set in a gothic–noir universe resembling the 19th century Eastern Europe, that is filled with original monsters, magic and weird technology.
The protagonist and his delightful ghostly companion have a wry sense of humor and contribute to the game’s atmosphere with many snappy dialogues. Especially the details in form of allusions to certain films, comics and the original book by Bram Stoker will keep you entertained.
The only shortcoming of this game is the rather stiff combat system, which would have needed more attention to establish a more fluent hack & slash feeling.
Estimated time for 100% completion: +100 hours
Singleplayer achievements: 95
Multiplayer achievements: none

I would wholeheartedly recommend this game! It is a great and unique take on things in what I would consider a mostly stale market.
The voices and mental aspect is extremely well done.
The combat, is excellent. I wouldn't call it simple by any means, but it is very cut and dry. Light, heavy, dodge and parry is all you have to work with, but if it ain't broke, don't fix it. Even though its simplistic, it is VERY tight and responsive. For an indy game, this combat feels better than almost any AAA title. I've heard some people liken it to DMC or other "hack n slash"  and it is very much not that. It isn't quite up to Dark Souls level of punishment, but each strike, block, and move has to be carefully thought out, especially against multiple opponents.
I refunded for two reasons, and one of those is actually a compliment.
First, I feel it is a bit of a walking simulator. I understand that this is just how the game works, but I felt just a little more tedious than a walking simulator should have been, for me at least. I don't mind walking, but I repeatedly found myself wandering around, quickly looking for solutions to walking puzzles and running through obstacles just to get myself to the next bit of juicy and amazing combat, or the next compelling bit of story.
The second is the main story mechanic, the voices, I think they nailed this aspect, and you never feel alone, or unwatched. I have actually met/known people with disorders similar (though not as bad) to Senua and their stories of how they describe things are eerily similar. To be plain, they did it too well for me, and I found myself very anxious and uneasy while I was playing, and for a short while afterwards. After playing long enough, I felt off enough that I wanted to stop playing.
To be honest, I think this would make a much better movie than a game. I found myself totally engrossed in Senua's tale, and wanted to know every twist and turn of events that happened to her, but the d@mn thing just unsettles me too much. I don't scare easliy, perhaps it was because this wasn't some fantastical world, but a very possible one inside someones head that was the difference, but this one certainly rustled my Jimmies.

TL; DR: Buy it on sale. I would recommend any price ~$15 or lower (I got it for $12.50) if you like good stories or beat-em-ups.
For those inclined to actually read into the details, I enjoyed this game, but let me get into why:
This game is in fact a beat-em-up. Not so much in the vein of the recent Batman games, but the combat is at least a little less vanilla than batman.
During combat, Nilin (the protagonist) has combos that she uses to take down enemies. The lower level enemies can be simply taken down with basic combos, but different levels of commanders normally accompany these grunts. Most of the commanders cannot be taken down directly and most of the time require a little bit of ingenuity to dispatch using Nilin's Sensen abilities. In short, when she fights or gets hit she gains focus meter (very similar to meter found in most fighting games) that allows her to do very strong abilities to help eliminate enemies. Most of the first playthrough you'll be using these on a *need* basis moreso than out of convience. However, you can upgrade the amount of meter you can hold and thus allows you to speed up progress.
On this subject, you'll be fighting one of about 5-6 kinds of bosses, most of which can be eliminated using the same tactics. Two pairs of bosses you'll fight will be identical--they can be eliminated exactly the same. It is a little stale, but there's about 8 boss battles, so you're not missing out on too much.
Most of the bosses do require a certain combonation of abilities and moves. Don't be worried if you cannot figure out the formula as the game will happily point out an exploit, and you can go on your merry way.
The story is nice: it's not going to be the next Hollywood film or anything but there were a couple of twists in there that were appreciated. The story did seem to drag on towards mission 7 (out of 8) but quickly picked up for the final mission.
Hidden items: There are a few. One of them increases health and is quite common while the other increases the meter mentioned earlier. The last is nonbenificial and is a hidden item for the sake of being a hidden item.
Overall: It's an RPG meant for the modern crowd. I would sort of compare it to the latest Deus Ex in that it is dumbed down quite a bit but unlike Deus Ex this game is stupidly linear. This game was a fun experience: since I just completed my first playthrough I plan on gettng the hidden items and then leaving the game alone. I would expect ~15 hours after all unlockables and that should be that.
TL; DR #2: Buy it for cheap. Good, but not exceptional.

Remember Me takes place in Neo-Paris in the year 2084, where mankind has developed the technology to digitalize people's memories to the point that we can remove and insert memories into people's heads and store them in a literal memory bank. Apparently (I'm not entirely sure why) this technology leads to the situation where the rich become richer and everyone else turns in to Roswell-style alien people. You play a woman called Nilin who was in the revolution against this technology, but gets caught and sent to jail, where her memories are stripped from her. She is broken out and you have to try and get your memories back and continue your revolutionary ways.
There is a focus on the prisons of the future as that is involved in the story, but I was rather intreaged about how the prisons work in this world. Basically your memories are removed from you and you're left in a situation where the prison is your whole world and so there is no desire to break out as you do not observe a world outside the prison. Then at the end of your sentence, your memories are given back to you and you don't remember your time in prison. This last part confused me as I would have thought that you would want to remember your time in prison so you have something to not want you to go back there, but that's my opinion. It would have been nice to see how other things are different in this world, like the education system, just for curiosity.
My favourite gaming mechanic in this game is the ability to change memories. Nilin seems to be the only person to have the ability to change people's memory, which is used rather sparingly. This mechanic involves seeing the original memory, and then going throught the memory and make small changes, like knocking over a bottle or retracting a coffee holder, in order to completely change the outcome, occuring in an apparent change in personality at times, which is a bit wierd.This mechanic is very fun to do, but there are only four throughout the whole game. To be fair, there is discussion about the morality of changing people's memory for your own personal gain, which may explain why it isn't used often, but I would really like it to have done it more.
The fighting mechanic annoyed me immensely at points. The general fighting scenarios is just punching and kicking a lot with a few special abilities. There is the option to stylize some combos so that some punches are more powerful or heal you and such, but I never really finished a seven attack long combo due to avoiding enemies so I didn't find much use in them. One of the most annoying bit about fighting is the length of them. I didn't really like it that in some fights I had to fight five waves of bad guys, spend about ten seconds of not fighting and then put into another fight scenario. There was also some rather harsh parts of fighting as well. There was one section where a big mech was performing a large AoE attack in a small area which I found hard to attack, and then show his weak point only at that point. The fighting section in all didn't really wow me, but it might suit someone who prefers fighting in games.
All in all, the three things that would get the player to play until the end is the memory changing gameplay, the well made sceneries and possibly the story if you're really into it. Otherwise you are left with a almost generic runny, jumpy, punchy game where the punchy happens a bit too much.

Remember Me is, most of the time, a third-person brawler with a strong narrative. However, it also contains some exploratory gameplay during its "memory remix" segments. The whole game adheres to the theme of memories, in both narrative and gameplay, which is very nice.
Levels are linear, alternating some platforming, and "arenas" where you must fight groups of enemies. The platforming parts are not very hard, but that is complemented by the challenges of finding all hidden upgrades and bonuses. Combat is based on customizable combos, which are built by setting specific attacks on a combo template. The end result is very fluid and accomodates different play styles. Finishing long combos grants a bonus of PMP, which is like "experience points" used to unlock new attacks. Therefore, the system rewards player's strategy and skill.
The narrative is another strong suit in Remember Me, receiving much positive criticism. The main characters are likeable, even if Nilin feels somewhat empty and bland during part of the game. The scenario of Neo-Paris is very detailed and visually well-done. The level of technology presented threatens to bring the narrative into the realms of fantasy, but I still found it acceptable to allow the exploration of the theme. The plot, if not the most innovative in its structure and elements, is still consistent and well presented. In my opinion, the rhythm of the game is good, and it only feels to be stalling at a point on its last third. With an average playtime of 10 hours, it could afford to lose an hour or so to keep sharp and engaging from start to finish.
The one real complaint I have about this game (and any other that uses the same technique) is the use of "quick time events." I can understand how these fit the theme of memory but still, they are very annoying and immersion-breaking, actually impairing the game experience.

A beautiful game. The concept is unique and the story telling makes you want to continue playing.
The combat system is implemented well and does have unique elements to it. There are different types of attacks that do different  actions. For instance, you have attacks, when connceted, heal you. You have attacks that will decrease your cooldown for special attacks and so on. The combat is very smooth. A good parallel would be the combat from the Batman Arkham games but with more customization.
The graphics are beautiful and really rich in atmosphere. I really had no complaints with them. Speaking of atmosphere, there are little things, such as retractng shop signs when you get close to them and little packs you can collect to learn more about the history that really enhance the game.
Audio is amazing. Voice acting is done well and you can really feel the emotions in the characters.
I read people had issues with the controls. I played with the XBOX 360 controller and had no issues. I don't know how the controls are on the keyboard, but I've heard that people have played it with mouse and keyboard without issues. Try both options if you can.
The storyline is what kept me playing through this game. There were just so many questions that needed to be answered and the game does wrap it up nicely in the end. The whole concept of memory management is amazing and implemented nicely in memory remixes, where you alter the memory of an individual. I don't want to ruin anything by saying more but the whole concept is flat out amazing and different.
Buy this game. It borrows elements from other games but also implements its own to provide an amazing package. We need more unique games like this and it all begins when you support them.
Truly worth playing from every angle.
P.S: It took me ~11 hours to complete the game but there is reason to go back, such as finding all the 'culture' packs and other collectibles.

The memory remixing scenes were a quite interesting feature which I never saw before in a game. I also heared some people complain about the game being too short or too easy. In my oppinion this is at least not true for the hard mode and if you don't just ignore the nice environments.

This game really surprised me. You can tell that a lot of love went into this game. The environments are pretty detailed and often look astonishing. Some textures could have had a higher resolution, but overall this game looks really good. The art design has good aesthetics that remembered me a little bit of Mirrors Edge (although Remember Me is way more detailed).
The normal background sound was good but nothing too fancy. The combat music, however, was really well made. It adapted to the situation really well and often made the fights really epic.
The fights are good, although nothing too spectacular, except, of course, for the boss fights. These were all pretty well staged and had their own mechanics, which you have to figure out. You cannot get stuck, as the game gives you hints or the solutions when you take too long.
The controls mostly work pretty well (played with keyboard and mouse). The only real exception is the spammer tool. This locks on to possible targets, which is of course helpful. In several fights you need to use it on certain enemies and although you look directly at them it targets another one. But if you know this problem, you can easily adapt to it and it will only be a small annoyance. A little bit more annoying was the camera, that sometimes (not too often) glitched or did not show all the enemies around you.
I played the game on high difficulty (because I read several times, that it would be too easy otherwise) and really enjoyed it. Don't get me wrong, this difficulty level will really be hard for most people, so expect to die often (especially during the boss fights). It was a challenge, but definitely a feasible one. Whenever I died, I knew exactly what I did wrong. It was never bad luck or bad controls.
I found the story entertaining and definitely better compared to a lot of other games (but there are better stories out there). I liked the memory remixes, where you can alter several things and you have to find a certain combination to achieve your goal.
So, all in all, there are several new and good ideas in this game with a few things that could be improved. If there will be another part I will most definitely buy it.

First, I have to say: I love breakout games.
Arkanoid, Batty, TRAZ, Krakout on C64 and the "newer" ones on Windows like
Warkanoid, Reaxxion (Steam), Ricochet Infinity, DX-Ball.
Even the 1978 version of the ORIGINAL Super Breakout in Arcade!
Why? Because the listed ones have their own charm.
Arkanoid have the style (especially the SNES version Revenge of the Doh, that's AWESOME!),
Batty have the "friendly family" feeling (2 player mode co-op), TRAZ is CRAZY.
Krakout is weird (but loveable), Warkanoid...beautiful, Reaxxion and Ricochet Infinity have the fast pace. DX-Ball: lots of levelpacks. Super Breakout? Simple.

Your goal is to hit an up-down moving heart with your ball.

You can choose your "Stick" (BAT!!!), helps a little bit but not much.
I can live without "powerups" in a breakout-style game. This mode has only
"Extra ball" and live, which technically only a ball. Because you can shoot more than one ball (you WILL) and if you lost your last ball (life): game over. Yeah, but the problem is:
the game still going!...You have to manually exit the game!

(tried the "set time" trick, doesn't work)
2 player mode? It's only a PONG in versus mode. A really trashy one. Not co-op!

Yepp, it has. Sometimes when you hit the ball with the edge of the bat, the ball FLIES out of the field and you loose it.

In a "ball game", it's a very important thing.
We don't need PhysX kind of, just a proper one.

Lame... In the mid 90's, it could be an okay as a shareware game for your Windows 95. Maybe.

Oh, MirrorMoon EP. Well, let me first start off that this game isn't for everyone. I recieved the game through a HumbleBundle purchase and seemed like a cool concept to try out. Started this game at 6 a.m. and completed it 100% 7.6 hours later. I was confused as hell what to do in the game in the begginning, until I researched video's and discussions about the general gist of the game and decided, "Here goes nothing."
I was able to start the panel first try and popped in the Side A  floppy diisk which ported me into a planet that seems to be the "Tutorial Mission". Takes you roughly 10 minutes to complete and realize that it is a puzzle game without any instructors, freeing your imagination. Once completing the "Tutorial Mission", the floppy disk turns over to Side B giving you the general content of the game. You must travel in light speed from Star to Star and discover unnamed ones that you can call it whatever you wish.  The core concept is to find planets with constellations in the sky that give you a map to where the "End game" level is.
When playing on the online part of the game, you actually work with everyone in that "Season" to discover stars and locate the "End Game" star. Very simplistic game that does not explain itself nor should it have to. If you want a game that tells you everything on what to do and what the plot/concept/end result is, then you have no creatvity nor want to explore. After all, this is a Space Exploration Puzzle Game.
In my opinion. I would rate it:
8/10 for Creativity
9/10  for Simplistic (No Man Sky) feel Graphics and Atmostphere.
6/10 for Online Content and Story
Overall, a solid 7 or 8 in my book. Doesnt hurt to purchase the bundle now and recieve 7 games for 6 bucks (about 80 cents a game people!) to try this bad boy out. Other than that, I would wait for sales and the price to go down to below 5 bucks.

Wow, this game is, frankly, amazing. I dithered over getting it for ages because the screenshots looked a bit meh, and finally caved over the Steam sale after looking at the reviews. And it's one of the few games I'm being slow about finishing purely because I don't want the experience to end. Those screenshots really don't do the the credit it deserves.
It's jaw-droppingly beautiful, taking into account both the music and the artwork, particularly the backdrops. After having gone through a fair amount of rubbish artwork over the last couple of decades as developers have tried to catch up with improving graphic capabilities, the kinds of scenery and other artwork going into modern 2D platformers is, frankly, amazing - Giana Sisters, Trine, Ori etc just look so good. The story isn't a Tolstoy epic, of course, but plucks at the heart-strings just enough whilst having a a villain that you both dislike and empathise with.
And the gameplay is spot on. Essentially metroidvania but the controls are pretty tight, it's classic and fun platforming, keeping it simple enough that it's accessible but there are some tough spots which actually feel rewarding to get through (rather than rage-inducing to the point of it being a slog). Like every time I tried I'd get a little bit further, make a mistake and work out how to get further still. It could not be better.

This horror action-adventure puts you inside the mind of Senua, a Celtic warrior on a vision quest into Viking Hell. Senua is living with psychosis. A gaming experience like no other, this story-rich journey is steeped in Norse mythology conveyed through flawless voice acting and awe-inspiring visuals (perceived through the prism of Senua's mental condition). Although the game is serene at times, much of it is turbulent, violent and disturbing.
The game has a fighting system which, while not revolutionary, is certainly competent. You learn most of the combat control elements early on in the game. Combat depth will gradually expand as new types of enemies reveal themselves. Once you learn how to succeed against each type of foe individually, the game will pit your fighting skills against various combinations of opponents. The key to success in those situations lies in mastering spacial awareness. The boss battles are meaningful and satisfying. I think it would be fair to describe Hellblade's combat system as somewhat reminiscent of Dark Souls, but more forgiving.
The game also features environmental puzzles which call for you to seek out certain patterns in order to advance. Although I am not naturally drawn to puzzles, I like how they were implemented in this game. Their difficulty felt about right and they did not feel contrived.
I can honestly say that I have never been so thorougly absorbed by a game before. I felt completely invested in Senua's struggle. I wholeheartedly recommend this gaming experience, as long as you do not object to themes of horror, violence and mental illness.
PS: I am bewildered by Steam's user-defined tag system, but Hellblade is definitely NOT a "Walking Simulator".

This game really surprised me. You can tell that a lot of love went into this game. The environments are pretty detailed and often look astonishing. Some textures could have had a higher resolution, but overall this game looks really good. The art design has good aesthetics that remembered me a little bit of Mirrors Edge (although Remember Me is way more detailed).
The normal background sound was good but nothing too fancy. The combat music, however, was really well made. It adapted to the situation really well and often made the fights really epic.
The fights are good, although nothing too spectacular, except, of course, for the boss fights. These were all pretty well staged and had their own mechanics, which you have to figure out. You cannot get stuck, as the game gives you hints or the solutions when you take too long.
The controls mostly work pretty well (played with keyboard and mouse). The only real exception is the spammer tool. This locks on to possible targets, which is of course helpful. In several fights you need to use it on certain enemies and although you look directly at them it targets another one. But if you know this problem, you can easily adapt to it and it will only be a small annoyance. A little bit more annoying was the camera, that sometimes (not too often) glitched or did not show all the enemies around you.
I played the game on high difficulty (because I read several times, that it would be too easy otherwise) and really enjoyed it. Don't get me wrong, this difficulty level will really be hard for most people, so expect to die often (especially during the boss fights). It was a challenge, but definitely a feasible one. Whenever I died, I knew exactly what I did wrong. It was never bad luck or bad controls.
I found the story entertaining and definitely better compared to a lot of other games (but there are better stories out there). I liked the memory remixes, where you can alter several things and you have to find a certain combination to achieve your goal.
So, all in all, there are several new and good ideas in this game with a few things that could be improved. If there will be another part I will most definitely buy it.

One of the best games I've played in a while. The combat can get a bit samey and tedious toward the end because of certain enemies that require you to use attacks with long cooldowns and mobs of smaller enemies interrupting your combos, but that's really my only complaint. It's a unique concept, striking visuals, a good story with a few holes. I strongly recommend it.

Ultimately, "Remember Me" is a game of squandered opportunities. Only two ingredients are without major flaws: The sound design is unique, dynamic and pitch-perfect as it mixes orchestral sound with futuristic glitching and staccato into something truely memorable - no pun intended. Nearly as perfect is the visual and world design: In the dystopic Paris of 2084 everything is overlayed by interface pop-ups integrated seamlessly into the world. The city is seperated into the immensly wealthy and deliberately ignorant upper class living in (also visual) luxury and the filth ridden slums haunted by poverty and monsters. Robots are everywhere, working relentlessly and melting with the scenery.
So, what are the other parts lacking?
The
is mediocre. Single enemies are no threat at all and hordes only really when they can surround you, bosses on the other hand can be pretty frustrating, because they are either accompanied by waves of smaller allies or are immune to all but one of your attacks; and in the second half of the game usually both. Also more than once bosses are recycled.
Putting together combos is pretty good, but the buttons for each combo are fixed and you only get a total of 4 different combos throughout the game, leaving you with altering the effect each combo has, rather than really putting together your own. Also the targeting becomes tedious with more than three enemies, because your current target is not indicated in any way and when dodging you sometimes jump away from the enemy instead of over them and thus breaking your combo.
The
is really lackluster. Though it usually works smoothly, there is no sense of challenge; the game even indicates via pop-up, where to go next. There is hardly any timing, puzzling or exploration needed, merely follow the breadcrumbs layed out for you until you reach your destination.
Though its design and visuals are stunning, the
is merely a beautiful scenery. You are railroaded through the platforming segments, the fight segments usually have a large arena to fight in and inbetween are (very good) cutscenes. There is hardly anything to deviate from that path aside from the casual lore, health or focus pick-up, which usually only involves following a short path to its dead end, where the pick-up lies.
From here on:
The
of the story, world and character development is much too fast. You can literally feel that underneath all those rushed moments could have been a very intense story: Tommy has maybe ten minutes of total screen time and his bar is visited twice before being wrecked, instead of building it up as a hub for the first half of the game so that its loss actually can mean something to the player. After that Tommy is not seen again, either. Olga, an assassin turned ally by remixing her memory, is seen twice in the game, too - the second time only to drop you off - instead of actually doing something with her. She could have regained her memory and turned on you, for example.
The
and
are the most solid, but still a bit shallow. You never truely get any backround on anyone, in Nilins case that is the whole point, but why, most importantly, have her parents stay so pale as characters. Yes, you get some info on them and personal background, but really just enough to make the story work.
The
are brilliant, very well executed, visually enthralling and serve as a kind of "boss fight" each time - which is a very good and alternative way to climaxe the tension of a level. But: There are only four in the entire game and two share the same elements (but done in a very good way!). Not only do you get information about the person you are remixing, but also see their motivations and crucial moments. This is, what the game would have needed more of, not excessively, but maybe six or seven such segments (combined with a longer playtime). Also, these sequences were kept rather simple, a bit more complex and extensive manipulation would have lent them more depth and actual qualities of a puzzle; but they are rather trial and error, just change stuff and see what happens. You don't get the feeling of actually understanding how to successfully remix a memory.
Overall, this is a game with so many good ideas and elements, that it is hard not to recommend, but at the full price point of 40€ it simply isn't. It has squandered too much of its potential, yet the simple fact that it does have that potential and you can feel it underneath its shell, leads me to say: Play it anyway! You will be entertained more than let down. Just know that it is the super-linear, story-driven game with merely okay combat that it is.
Verdict: Recommendable for outstanding art design, both visual and audio, but sadly not at full price!

I had originally thought that the game was missing something around the missions between NYC and Roswell, Grace felt like a ham fisted rushed attempt to get a game out to ride the coat tails of the current faux out rage of the month.
It gets far worse, this game is a mess. Gimmicks, story, game play and tone.
For one I liked the gimmick that BJ was weakened by the events of Wolflenstien 1 so your health didn’t regenerate fast and you could only stay at half health, but that got old after a while, thats a fine gimmick for the first few hours not half the game.
Speaking of gimmicks, the game has 2 way you’re going to encounter enemies a majority of time you either get clunky stealth hallway shooter or endurance hallway shooter...but yes the stealth part can turn into endurance shooter but this too gets old and repetitive.
Yes you get to ride a Phanzer Hound..for like 3 mins and you get to fight three and by fight I mean the first two pretty much stand there.
There’s side quest but they don’t give you anything except pad out the game length, literally nothing..you get a generic thanks.  The assassinations are just killing a random generic cannon fodder and server no real purpose except padding out the length of the game.
You get 3 options for enhancements, stilts to get to high places, shoulders to ram though enemies and obstacles and a chest piece that lets you get into tight places unfortunately they don’t serve much of a purpose except to give round about ways to get from point a to point b.  The game never has fun with them or use them to their full potential, they just felt either tacked on or an unfinished idea.
The story is a mess and I’m convinced this game was set to release next year but they rushed it out in since the mood in America at the time was free marketing.  So they slapped in stuff like meeting grace in Manhattan, stitched the game together in such a way that the story makes no sense or time flows like a kids scribble in this alternate time line.
You meet Grace and Super Spesh in the Empire State Building, save them from Nazis.  All 3 of you get on the U boat, Grace takes over the resistance.  You go to the lower decks of your u boat that has more Nazis hiding in it than Castle Wolflenstien..FOR SOME REASON no one bothered to do anything about them.  Get a nuke war head and are sent to Roswell to meet Super Spesh, who has set up a front in a Diner behind Nazis line complete with secret tunnels and conspiracy theorist trope basement...but the U boat never went to Roswell, actually the last you saw him he was on the u boat amazed he can poop in a toilet (not kidding)..but some how he was in Roswell this whole time or at least long enough to set up a front while also being in Manhattan with Grace?
You nuke the base in Roswell then later you find out because of this they moved it to Venus. This is passable since there’s no time line on how long it took to get your body...EXCEPT Anya still hasn’t given birth.
Side note about Roswell, it’s played up like the Nazi’s have alien technology and secret experiments, which Nazis did do experiments on people.  You’d figure this would be at least an interesting section of the game maybe get a fun weapon..wait nope just an industrial elevator shaft shooting gallery.
Back to Grace, where to start, there’s two Graces.  The one you meet in Manhattan who’s completely blind to whats going on around her, who’s she’s talking to and what they’ve done IN CONTEXT OF THE GAME WORLD. I don’t really want to go that far into it since I only have a limited space.  Then there’s Grace at the half way point who comes off more grounded in reality but still passionate not the idiot who wonders why we didn’t nuke everyone with no target cause white men are evil except the one who’s doing all the heavy lifting.
Then it happened, Sigrun snaps and calls Grace out on her racism and it hit me. Grace isn’t some SJW soap box for the devs, either the whole Manhattan back and forth with BJ was shoved in to rush the game out (which explains the Super Spesh inconsistency) or she’s like a South Park parody of the far-left SJW tumblr types.
It’s strange that people seem to focus on her being the “Strong female character if you hate you’re a alt right fox news watcher” but not the preggo bad♥♥♥♥♥topless drenched in Nazi blood Anya.
I liked the back story of BJ and while I enjoyed his monologue of accepting his mortality that was great at the end of TNO not for HALF of TNC...it gets old and whiny.  It was great to grow with BJ to be a bad♥♥♥♥♥killing machine and at the end showing his vulnerability, it’s a great hero arch.  It comes off whiny and stale when it’s half a game.
Then there’s the end..or should I say “to be continued in DLCS”. The basis of this game was to take back America, but it ends with Grace BJ and a few really under developed characters telling people it’s time to take back America.  You know the trailer where you hear grace give the rise up speech..thats THE END!? In TNO you had a great build up to a fun fight with death’s head in Wolf2 is press middle mouse to win. Thats how you kill Frau Engle, there’s no stand off no back and forth no chase nothing just “Hi BJ..I deed”.
The final boss is a game of peak-a-boo with generic Nazi cannon fodder bullet sponges.  A fight I’ve done ad nauseam at this point in the game.  You steal a ship thats going to stop the Nazi’s..in an upcoming DLC.
Maybe I’m wrong in expecting there to be a revolution in a game touted to be about taking back America from Nazis not setting up a revolution that will come in 6 months for $24.99...maybe..
Then there’s “the key with no lock” you never find out what thats for, it’s mentioned at the end but then the game just ends.
The tone is all over the place too, first it starts off somber and kind of depressing with the hero facing his own mortality, starts to get into the absurd fantasy of the originals and hints towards the Nazis and secrets in area 51 which ends up being nothing then goes back to somber with BJ having a “I know I’m going to die so let me remember my past”  moment to full-on John McClain but nope a dream so back to somber to a robocop reference to SUPER SOLIDER ACTION MAN everyone is happy! Then while A51 was grounded in reality you go see Hitler on Venus right into a “before the last mission” scene from SR3 and SR4.
Speaking of Hitler..you’d figure since this was a game about ending the Nazi occupation of America, or was supposed to be you would figure you would kill Hitler while on Venus..NOAP! Thats another DLC I assume, you’re rather fight the shooting gallery hallway of forced stealth.
Also, what was the colossus?  It's a reference to the Statue of liberty but that seems tacked on, I assumed it would have to do with the last fight with Engle but that was just hit middle mouse to win..
It could have been a great game, there’s the foundation for a great game, but it’s just that a foundation and to think this is Bethesda focusing on a single player experience.

Father.

I had a very difficult childhood.
Some of you might know that growing up as an only child is not much of an entertaining childhood, but the part that made it all even worse was growing up fatherless. I can still remember my mother bathing me every night, feeding me or taking me to school. I kept asking myself "Why can't my dad be here?". He missed every important event of my life, all of it. I hated him at the time, or at least, wanted to hate him.
Dads fail many times, and in some cases they really ♥♥♥♥ up. My little story might be also your case or a part of your life where you really wanted to hate the person that originated you. Shower With Your Dad Simulator 2015 showed me much more than just a game. I immediately felt the connection between myself and the past, which I could only dream of; a dad, who is always there to run to. And no matter how I tried, I can't truly hate my father even if he screwed up, nor I can change the past. The only thing I can work on now, is being a dad who's there to bathe, feed and ready to grow old with his own children one day.

It's great for the old-school fighter. Those of us that grew up on Street Fighter II/CE/Turbo/Alpha, Mortal Kombat 1, 2, and 3, TMNT Tournament Fighters, and pretty much any SNK title. Those of us that also grew up on games like Streets of Rage, Double Dragon, and Final Fight will also find a lot to love.
However, those that grew up on 3D fighters and the current generation of 2D fighters won't be as big of fans of this game. The action is pretty fast-paced, but it's more along the lines of you have to practice with *your* character and get good before you take your game online or set the game to the "nightmare" difficulty.
Graphics - 10/10
I love hand-drawn anything, and fluid animation at 60+fps. Keep in mind that you do have to set the resolution to what your video card or IGP can do; don't expect a GeForce 8600 GTS or an Intel Iris Pro to run the game at 1080p with 3D scrolling turned on, but my Hackintosh running 10.10.4 had no problems with a GTX 760 running this at 1080p.
Audio/Music - 9/10
Sound effects fit and music is pretty well done, but those voices get a little annoying at times.
Controls - 9/10
Tight, the way they should be. It's close to how the SFII games were on SNES and Genesis, where everything reacts immediately.
Replayability - 7/10
I have a feeling that once I beat this, it'll only come out when I'm in a mood to play a fighter and KoF XIII isn't what I want to play.
Overall - 8/10
Not something I'd pay fifteen dollars for, but if you find it in a Humble Bundle or on sale for under ten, it'll be worth it, as long as you're an old-school fighter fan. For those that are new-school fighter fans, I'd read through other reviews to see what others think of the game.

Wow, this game is, frankly, amazing. I dithered over getting it for ages because the screenshots looked a bit meh, and finally caved over the Steam sale after looking at the reviews. And it's one of the few games I'm being slow about finishing purely because I don't want the experience to end. Those screenshots really don't do the the credit it deserves.
It's jaw-droppingly beautiful, taking into account both the music and the artwork, particularly the backdrops. After having gone through a fair amount of rubbish artwork over the last couple of decades as developers have tried to catch up with improving graphic capabilities, the kinds of scenery and other artwork going into modern 2D platformers is, frankly, amazing - Giana Sisters, Trine, Ori etc just look so good. The story isn't a Tolstoy epic, of course, but plucks at the heart-strings just enough whilst having a a villain that you both dislike and empathise with.
And the gameplay is spot on. Essentially metroidvania but the controls are pretty tight, it's classic and fun platforming, keeping it simple enough that it's accessible but there are some tough spots which actually feel rewarding to get through (rather than rage-inducing to the point of it being a slog). Like every time I tried I'd get a little bit further, make a mistake and work out how to get further still. It could not be better.
If you like platformers then this is damned good.

I've never played a more emotionally impactful or visually stunning platformer than Ori and the Blind Forest. The intro alone had me half in tears with a hand slapped over my mouth. No, I didn't realize what I was getting myself into. I highly recommend curling up at night with your favorite headphones and disappearing into Nibel, the world of this game, and climbing through this vivid and colorful (and at times thrillingly scary) landscape. The gameplay is intuitive, quick to learn, and deceivingly simple. The world is ripe with secrets and twisting paths, built in the way where you'll revisit previous areas with your new abilities to reach the far-away spots that you couldn't before, a la Metroid or Castlevania. The challenging parts (like frantically escaping up a shockingly fast-filling hollow tree amidst crashing waves and heartrending music) will have your blood pumping and your jaw dropped in a stupor. Did I mention the immersive and thoroughly inspired soundtrack that grips you from the start and never lets go, seamlessly dancing with you from region to region, moment to moment? Please give yourself a slap in the face and make a mess of all your senses and #feels by introducing yourself to Ori today.

Ori and the Blind Forest is a beautiful and has a story of friendship, selflessness, and loss. It's on a fundamental level, structured as so many other platformers are; It springs from the Metroid and Castlevania tradition, gating your progress behind doors that can only be opened once you have learned a particular skill. I highly recommend this game.
