Yes, we all know the hype, big promises, how the launch went and all those missing features etc. I did not jump in the hypetrain, I actually very much didn't like or even understood the core idea of the game back then. And I hated the style of the graphics.
But as a scifi fan, I followed the news and some mild interest started to form, nevertheless at the same time I was being sceptic. I was sure the game could not possibly deliver all those features they were talking about. Or could it? Well, after the launch when reading first impressions and reviews I was, even when not expecting too much, disappointed. A little surprised too, "Oh, it came out to be THAT bad?"
I was not going to buy this game. I have limited time to spend on games and these kind of games usually take a lot of it. No way I'm going to use my precious freetime to play time consuming, let alone bad games.
Then came the Foundation update. With base building. And survival mode. And I decided, for some reason, to buy the game.
And I'm very, very glad I did. Because it is almost nothing like I thought after reading all the bashing. I jumped right down to the deep end and started with survival-mode. Later I tried normal-mode and a brief test confirmed, that Survival is where this game really gives everything it has to give and all the well thought out mechanics and gameplay loops are in use. And this is important. Very important. In normal mode flying your ship is basically free, money and resorces come in faster than you can spend or store, you are constantly finding new tech, blueprints, bases... This means money loses its meaning. Exploring loses it's meaning. And for example rover is useless, why would you drive anywhere if you can fly there? You don't need to worry about plutonium, you literally stumble upon it everywhere you go. I can see that normal mode works for others, but I also see that it is part of the NMS's problem because it makes the game too easy and pointless. Fortunatelly, it all changes in Survival-mode.
In the beginning of the Survival you are constantly fighting for your life and low on everything. You need to plan your moves very carefully. At the same time you need to repair your gear and try to make your way to your ship and repair that too. It was an awesome experience, and when you are finally sitting in cockpit, ship repaired, filled up and ready to go, you really feel a great sense of accomplishment. But it does not stop there. Every take off needs a FULL tank of plutonium. So you need to carefully consider is certain place or planet worth landing. This is one of the things that greatly impact on the game experience on survival vs normal mode. You just can't proceed as fast as in normal because you can't land everytime you see something interesting on the ground. Also every new discovery feels fresh and instead of "discovered new place every other minute" there might go hours before you see a base, outpost or shelter of any kind. And that's awesome.
I remember this one time when I rushed to this small outpost, again just barely making it. Environment shield died a few seconds before I made it through the door and inside. There was one alien and he had cool looking multi-tool on the wall. I looked at it and checked the prize, whoooa, over three million credits. Bit more than my 200 000cr which I was able to scourge together so far. It would take a while to be able to buy that kind of stuff when I was barely keeping my self alive... I decided to talk to the alien before I go, if I was lucky he might give me some blueprint or something. I walked to communicate with the alien and he wanted to see my own, still basic multi-tool. Cool, maybe he makes a mod or something, but no. He took my multi-tool and gave me that 3000000cr badass gear from the wall! It came completely out from the blue. Right now I can't rember ANY game, where one single gift or loot from a npc has felt so special and expensive. I will always remember that encounter with that friendly alien.
Fight for survival continues, even with the working ship and cool multi-tool. You still need to search resources and if there is a poi somewhere nearby, it is more economical to just try to walk there. Lots of people say that when you get your ship fixed, game becomes boring grind. Well, I certainly did not find it boring, exactly opposite. Game just starts.
It is far from boring grind. I don't play this game to reach center of the universe as fast as I can. I propably never get there. Instead my goal is to get rich, build huge base, buy freighter and cool ships, learn to "tame" the game universe. Make it my home. I've allready established a small base and am now able to drive a rover. It is very fun thing to drive and makes exploring planets much easier. And using it is much, much more cheaper than flying with your ship everywhere. You still need to do certain things, like resource scans on foot, though. But now you can cover those medium distance trips easily and unlike with a ship, you can search and collect everything on the way.
Well, of course the game is not perfect, far from it. I've encountered some bugs, and the game has crashed two times, which is annoying if you have lots of unsaved progress behind. Graphics are very good, but style still divides opinions. Animals could be more diverse and landscapes too, especially caves. But every now and then you encounter some truly cool planets and vistas that are out of the "norm", same goes with creatures. Space flying is lacking and controls are very basic, allthough pretty fun after you get used to them. Space stations are pretty forgettable, but now they are attleast crowded. And I agree, game needs a goal and more content for those who can't make their own. But as recent patches show, Hello Games actually started to deliver, so far with high quality content.
I've now spent 63 hours in the universe of NMS, more than on average game, and feel confident to say that I like NMS VERY much. It is not the game that was hyped, but it is a great game nevertheless! Exploring new planets, finding resources, meeting aliens, building your base, hiring staff, it all is very fun and rewarding experience. But I cannot stress enough, at least for me the game truly opened up in Survival-mode, Normal mode just smoothes out all the nice little details and mechanics in gameplay, those details that really make the game fun, varied and challenging.

Hellblade is an experience first and a game far second. You can think of this  as interactable artistic movie, but just one that cannot be watched like a movie can (it's a terrible choice for streaming, so don't even bother). To really "get it" you have to play if yourself. Interestingly game chooses not to display UI, which was a refreshing change from some recent games that fill the screen with information.
Gameplay aspects themselves are kind of lacking.
Combat is as easy as it can be. Even on hard difficulty this game is extremely lenient. You got a dodge with iframes, block button with easy parry timing, some simple comboes. Focus mechanic for slomo attacks and getting up from ground if you happen to get knocked down. Only reason you even get hit is usually the sticky auto-aiming that gets annoying when you are fighting multiple opponents. Oh, and you have health regeneration too. Again with the minimalist focus, this game has barely any tutorials beyond voices sometimes shouting you to dodge an attack and such.
Puzzles... Most are very simple. Couple fun puzzles/obstacles here and there, but most are just about walking to a spot and focusing. Solutions are quite evident in most cases right off the bat or within a minute or two of observation at most.
I'd recommend this to people who want an experience that might shock them a bit and for cool visuals and some light gameplay. Presentation is great. Audio is great. Animations are very good. Graphics look very nice and art direction is excellent.
NOT, I repeat, NOT recommended for those who want focus on more meaty gameplay. There are a lot of games that do that part better than Hellblade does. Just for example, you could get Hollow Knight instead if you want mix of story/exploration and straightforward combat.
I was ok with my purchase even with some disappointments on the game mechanic side, since the delivery was so strong, so I will give it a blue thumb. Your mileage WILL vary, however.

This is the first instalment of the Assassin's Creed Chronicles series, a 2.5D stealth platforming version of Assassin's Creed. It's clear that the developers extensively studied Klei Entertainment's indie hit Mark of the Ninja, and then appropriated most of its superficial characteristics (vision cones for enemies, sound detection, hiding places, etc.). Some stuff is expanded upon. For example, you can sometimes move deeper into the level, towards the background, or cross a beam and move forwards. Sometimes, when rounding a corner, the camera will switch round and change the perspective of the level.
Unlike Mark of the Ninja, the Assassin's Creed Chronicle games are a lot more linear. There's little in the way of exploration, and many situations clearly have an optimal solution. Sometimes, especially in the later instalments of this series (India, and particularly the third and weakest entry, Russia), you are completely railroaded to complete a situation *exactly* in the way that the level designer intended. In those instances, these games feel rather weak and more puzzle-like than anything in Mark of the Ninja, which allowed more room for creative solutions to problems, even if the main problem is always getting from the left side of the level to the extreme right.
Anyway, the games in this series look gorgeous, with period and culture-specific artwork, great sound and voice-acting, and generally solid gameplay (that is slightly marred by poor design choices in India and goes completely off the rails in Russia). If you have an interest in this series, I'd recommend China without any problems, even if Mark of the Ninja is still superior (and you should totally play that first if you haven't already). India is a decent follow-up, but I'd skip Russia.

The one thing that might be a downside to some people is that to really understand everything that's going on you should really play all the romance routes (and probably try all the bad endings as well), but honestly the game is so engaging that it didn't feel like a chore to me at all to go through all the routes and get the secret endings.
I know it looks like it's pricey, but honestly it could cost twice as much and still be worth it. Beautiful art, five very distinct romanceable characters, and an engaging storyline made this the perfect game.

After about 25ish hours I did finally manage to get all the good endings (I was too lazy to try and get all the bad endings. It's up to personal preference really on that aspect.)
Before I really get into the review, I would like to point out a few things first -
Like many VNs, the beginning portion is usually quite similar through each run, and then it branches off depending on who you have the highest affinity with. But with this game it has a nice mechanic that when you start the game, you kind of get to choose who you want to pursue. You have the choice of picking the Lance, Yeon-Ho, Yuri route (which begins with the same first few chapters despite small difference depending on the choices you choose, and then branching off with the guy you have the highest affection with.) and then you have the option for Tei and Red's route - which starts off completely different and the whole game plays out with your character pursing that one from the start. It's a similar mechanic to the Norn9 stuff, and it's up to preference. I know a lot of people like playing the game blind and then depending on the character's looks/personality/traits etc. they decide who they want to go for in the moment, but me, being a lazy person, I usually just pull up a walkthrough and go through it without much thought.
So I personally don't find that mechanic to be bad, but it's up to you.
Now, for the actual review!!
Nameless has a solid story that addresses many deeper topics such as abuse, abandonment, and loss. It handles these topics quite nicely, and leaves you with a better understanding of said topics.
It's not as 'metophoric' as some other games, but I personally think it's better because it really hits home how these situations affect others and even yourself.
To be bluntly honest, at around my second/third route I was beginning to get a little irritated with a few things, but the two secret endings overshadowed any of that left me in tears, which I think is enough.
Pros
- At first, each character seems to fit into each different archtype (cold silent type, loli, big brother, romatic, etc...) which seemed kind of lazy to me, but once you go down the paths you can see how much personality they actually have.
- The art is pleasing to the eye, and the character designs are unique and lovely.
- The story puts you on an emotional roller coaster. You will be laughing and having a grand old time one minute, and then crying the next.
- Each character is different. They have different flaws and different likes/dislikes. No character is 'perfect' which leaves them feeling human.
- In my case, I actually felt jealous and a little upset depending on different factors, which is another way that the game plays with your emotions - keeping you constantly enthralled in the story.
- The voice acting, especially for ??? is some of the best I've heard. Whenever ??? speaks I feel like I am feeling exactly what he is. The anguish, the sorrow, the anger... It is all perfectly conveyed through the voice actor.
Cons
- The protagonist, Eri, is a little 'too' innocent for me. Problems with simple solutions can take her chapters to fix. She always seems clueless and that kind of took me out of the story. In most situations she is fine and relateable, but in others I would find myself hitting my head against my desk because she was too innocent. (Incoming rant) I have dealt with clueless/innocent characters before, but they were different. Cardia (from Code: Realize) spent her entire life locked up in a mansion, so when she finally leaves it she doesn't know much of anything. The story made it so that there was a reason why she didn't know much of anything, so that kept it from being annoying. Another example is the Heroine from Amnesia Memories - she starts off the game with Amnesia so she doesn't know anything. Meanwhile, in Nameless, even though at some points Eri does experience amnesia, from the start she is very innocent without much reason to be. This might not be a problem for everyone, but it was just annoying for me. You don't notice it all the time, but when it did happen it was aggrivating.
- Like many different VNs translated to English, there are typos. Now, I've kind of grown used to this after years of playing different Visual Novels, so it doesn't bother me too much. It's not too often and even if it does break imersion for a few moments you can still understand what is going on.
All and all, I think this is a great Visual Novel for anyone who likes Otome or Cheritz. So if you have a passion for Visual Novels I really think you'll like it. A unique story, fun characters, great music and voice acting... It may not be the best one I have ever played, but it is definately up there!

I will admit, I bought this game out of curiosity after finishing Mystic Messenger. This game was definitely worth the buy. I had a lot of fun! This game had a unique spin with the whole doll aspect, but it was very enjoyable and I loved unfolding pieces of the full story with each route. My only complaint is that the female protagonist can be a bit cringey at times with how "slow" she is (as the boys put it), but it was easy to get over. All of the boys have very different personalities from each other which makes every route interesting. Personally, Red's route was my favorite. The prologue can seem long and the common routes (Yuri, Yeonho, Lance) can be a bit tedious in the beginning, but they're well worth it. I played in the order of Yuri - Lance - Yeonho - Tei - Red; I believe this order will allow for you to unveil parts of the story more naturally, and I think I had a fantastic experience by following this order. Overall, I enjoyed myself, and would probably play it over again in the future. I definitely recommend this to people getting into visual novel otome games after playing Mystic Messenger.

This game has so much potential to become a really enjoyable game, if only the main attractions were not a pain to use.
I will point out a few things and let you decide by yourself if this is worth your cash.
First: The camera is horrible, you have to hold the right mouse button to take the cursor out of the screen and make it follow the mouse movement, kinda like a third person game. And the camera movement is kinda bad too. I really wish there was an option to play it in first person.
Second: The vehicle and creatures control is also terrible, it depends on what direction the camera is pointing instead of what direction the vehicle is pointing, so if the camera is facing the front of the vehicle and you press W it will reverse. It will also turn as you tirn the camera. There are also many vehicles and creatures, wich is great, and you can ride most animals (even dragons) and all vehicles. There is also a plane, a helicopter, an excavator and a drill.
Third: Building things with bricks you unlock is also a pain, the camera movement is so bad it makes placing bricks unnecessarily hard. This should be the highest point and the main attraction of this game, because it has pretty much all the bricks that exist in the base lego sets (excluding technique, Bionicle, Mindstorm and such).
Fourth: The game has almost no objective, all you do is run around exploring and collecting things, wich can be pretty fun for a few hours, but after that the game becomes boring since there is nothing elso but trying to use the terible building system to build something. It can become really cool if you get used to it tho.
Fifth: Combat is cool, there is a nice variety of weapons and items that you can use, from rifles, swords, shields to dynamite and bananas, wich you can find in some big chests around the map. However, aiming with the ranged weapons is kinda bad, but you can get used to it.
Sixth: EVERYTHING is made out of bricks, save a few world objects and you can remove every single one of them, brick by brick. You can even blow up water and leave a hole in it.
Seventh: The ambients are really cool and beautiful, also, the world objects mentioned before can be placed after you unlock them, so you can build some really nice stuff.
So that is pretty much what i have to say about this game. I think it was worth my money because it was kinda cheap, but I really wish there was a mod or something that turned this into \"LEGO Minecraft\", that would pretty much take away everything negative about this game in my opinion (not because it would \"be\" Minecraft, but because it would adress everything I see as negative and make it more playable, give the game something to actually be done instead of just running around exploring and unlocking things and would also make building so much easier).

Let me say that the game is beautiful, and although the draw distance is low it does have a sense of endless scale. However, as big as the world is, right now there is nothing to do in it.
Exploring around and finding new characters and models is cool, but at the end of the day there is no purpose. Now, I would be ok with this if the model builder allowed more complex creations; i.e. cars, planes, etc. But as far as I can tell, the only vehicles are prefab and must be found and then purchased.
I remember a Lego game from the windows 98 era which, while it was a very small world to play in, allowed you to create anything you could imagine with wheels or wings or whatever. Even trains if I remember correctly.
As of right now the only things you can build is static models; houses, castles, whathaveyou.
I guess what I am feeling is that its like minecraft without any quests. Dont get me wrong, I dont want this to be like minecraft; if I wanted to I would just go play it. It doesnt need to be Lego minecraft, but some sort of quest/purpose system would make it fun.
Or allowing the manufacture of vehicles and ships. Lego pirates would be a good addition with all the water that seems to be generated in every world. Or aquanauts for underwater exploration. Those were some of the coolest models!
I cant knock it too bad, I know its early access, and I buy alot of early access games gambling on whether they will pan out into something. At this point, I cant find too many reasons to play the game, but hopefully the next update will include building moving models, some sort of quest system, and maybe ships or underwater vehicles.
For the price its worth a gamble, but keep in mind the current state will not offer much gameplay.

Right off the bat, I want to say that I hate having to click "No" under the recommendation option. I really, REALLY hate to because this is a really fantastic game. Unfortunately, is abhorrently relentless when it comes to CPU usage. I'm not sure if it's just my laptop's specifications or not, but I shall include them for the sake of establishing an understanding in the event someone points out the issue I may be missing, or if Lego elects to do so.
My specifications are as follows:
Intel core i7-3630QM @ 2.4 GHz
AMD Radeon HD 7870M
16 GB DDR3 RAM
About 1 TB HDD space; shared across 2 7200 rpm 500 GB HDDs
My OS is Windows 10, although it was originally 8 and I experienced the same issues.
Now, oddly enough, I do not experience lag during gameplay, in fact, the game runs extremely smoothly, which obviously is fantastic, it is quite lovely faffing about in a land of lego bricks.
The issue is, about 5 minutes after I begin playing my temperature monitoring software begins to complain of dangerously high CPU temperatures, and I've tweaked the settings quite a lot to try to cut down on things, but I get similar results no matter what combination of settings and restarts I test out.
I've read some forums that explain that staying in one place, instead of wandering about so that the game isn't having to continuously render bricks would fix the problem, however this has not been the case.
My temperature monitoring software regularly reports temperatures around the neighborhood of 80-90 degrees Celcius, which can cause severe residual damage over a period of time. Also  Task Manager reports that the game runs my CPU at 99% while it is running, which no other program I've used in the history of owning this laptop has been able to accomplish.
I know the game is still Early Access, and I'm sure that there are a few optimization issues that still need to be ironed out, which is why I don't want to be harsh in this review. This is the ONLY complaint I can think of with this game, and that's why it's rather painful to give it such a negative review.
The environments are beautiful and fun to explore, the build tools are rather easy to use, and overall it is really nice, I just have my fingers crossed in hopes that these issues are resolved soon.

If you are a strategy fan, it is hard to go wrong with this game.  Countries of different sizes, locations, tech groups, religions all make for lots of replayability.  It's a long game, and can eat away hours at a time in a single play session.  The Complete includes all the expansion packs which added new mechanics and modified the vanilla game.
Perhaps my favorite thing about the game is there is always something to do.  Long term goals may be to become the biggest superpower, best trader, largest colonial empire, or perhaps take over the world (muhahaha), but each play session you have shorter term goals to get there, from increasing your tech to balancing your economy, to forging alliances, to converting the heretics within your nation.  A lot of fun, and one of the best values for my gaming dollars.

After all its expansions, it's probably the best game by Paradox in terms of balance, complexity and fun. Mods like MEIOU made it the king of Grand Strategy, with a level of depth and replayability that still compete with its successor EUIV today. Great game, great legacy.

There is not a single "flaw" that makes No Man's Sky a "bad game" - the sum of want was delivered just did not add up to what was promised.
First of all, some of the features promised were not included at all: It was implied that you could meet other players (unlikely as it were in the wide universe), but that was disproven only a few hours after launch. No Man's Sky is singleplayer, no matter what it tries to pretend otherwise, and you will never meet any other living soul ingame. Also look at the third trailer in the top (the one with the dinosaurs) - did you expect some kind of natural-looking ecosystem like that in the game? Nope, there is not, this was all "staged" for the trailer.
Secondly, the UI - it was/is clunky to use. Landing and launching take some time during which you can do nothing, so hopping from place to place on a planet with your ship is more toil than anything else - imagine it as short unskippable cutscenes every few minutes. Yeah, fun. Also did you hope to fly only meters from the ground? Forget it - if you want to go lower than several hundred meters you need to land.
Lastly, the big selling point was the infinite potential of the game - each world procedurally generated, always something new... Unfortunately it is not - after a few planets the game gets a "sameish" feeling to it, sure the trees are blue now instead of red, and that critter has stripes - but essentially it feels like the very same content recycled over and over and over ad nauseatum.
So my verdict: if you can buy it for 10$ or so, you might get your money's worth for the few hours you might play it, otherwise best stay away.

On the Surface, The Incredible Adventures of Van Helsing is a pretty good, solid indie ARPG. It's inexpensive, often on sale, has great graphics and voice acting for an indie game, and scratches that loot, level up and kill itch these games tend to do. TIAVH borrows elements from Torchlight II including limited class selection, an activatable rage mode to use spell power ups and a companion that can engage in combat,collect loot, store loot and buy potions from town stores. The gothic/steampunk UI looks sharp and fits the world perfectly. Gear has a nice, unique, though sometimes slightly annoying ehancement system called Essence - so instead of having Gem slots/sockets, gear has a limited capacity of Essence Pieces that have a varying effects and Essence points. There is a perk system that allows the player to choose a permanent buff every time they level up in Reputation. Another unique mechanic of the game is the optional Tower Defense style combat sections. There's also a Scenario mode that lets you play special maps and earn permanent buffs to your account, much like Badass Points from Borderland 2, provided you reach level 27, which unfortunately, I have not. For the most part, the core gameplay is pretty similar to any well recieved ARPG.
Unfortunately, while the core is solid, the exterior is damaged by various problems that eventually ended my enjoyment of the game.
Many players reported the combat being a little repetitive. While I think there are enough varied enemies with an array of different attacks, the end result of each encounter was almost exactly the same - Find a horde of 10+ enemies that swarm you in a instant, requiring you to infinitely kite them around spamming the same 2-4 spells/tricks. This didn't bother me, even up to my final moments with the game, but it is something to note if the repetition sounds annoying to you and is a problem in this game due to a limited hotbar key assignments - likely a symptom of the console cross-platform development (this game was developed for Xbox 360). However, the lack of an extended hotbar meant that I could only reliably use 6 total skills and meant that I didn't bother with getting new ones, since they couldn't be used efficiently. While you do have a second hotbar with the Tab button, this doesn't work well in practice as you may lose access to some of your more helpful skills (like slowing time or a heal spell) to make room on a second bar with skills that you don't use often (which in turn are probably weaker because you didn't invest ability points into them). Torchlight II had a similar mechanic, but it still let you use 1-0 instead of 1-4. I understand that the design means I don't have to jump my hands all over the keyboard like other ARPGs, but it also meant that I had less usability and mostly relied on the same couple of skill the entirity of the game.
You are also stuck with one class, the Hunter (Warrior type), unless you by DLC for The Thaumaturge (Mage) and/or Archane Mechanic (Summoner, maybe Ranged/Rogue as well). However, there a variety of spells and potential builds for each class and the complete package and DLC are often on sale. I bought the package before even realized that the other classes were behind a paywall.
One of the biggest issues are bugs, which tend to vary quite widely depending on the player.  Minor bugs I ran into where graphical gltiches with my mage spells and sometimes, I don't think all the math on gear adds up quite correctly. My biggest bug is where I had a four enemy boss battle which never activated after the cutscene, so the enemies just stood their not attacking and could not be harmed as well. I had to use a console command to remove the quest from my Journal, but I still couldn't kill the bosses. I've stopped playing after that point and came back to the game many months later and it still was not fixed. The devs do appear to update the game quite frequently and they deserve credit for that, but technical issues are reported often on the forums. Laregely, nothing was game breaking besides that one boss battle and I was still able to play a large chunk (maybe the majority) of the game before I quit with out other major issues.
The nail in the coffin for me was the fact that once I reached Old Town, I died WAY to frequently. I died relatively often in this game before because I was playing Hard difficutly with a glass cannon mage, but despite even pushing more Attribute points and gear to increase my health and defense, I would often die to one hit kills and my "Glass cannon" build didn't have a reliable AOE attack or way to survive - most enemies are too fast to outrun and if we couldn't kill them, we died. It was more like a "Glass Rifle" build. While this problem is possibly due to my difficulty and build, the idea in these games is that any build should be viable in this type of game, and since my only possible strategy was kiting enemies that were too fast for me, there was nothing else I could do to advance (short of abusing the respawn system to advance) and I lost interest. Thank goodness I didn't play Hardcore.
This game is a prime example of why Steam reviews needs a "Maybe" recommendation option. There is a lot of good here that I spent 20+hrs with, but utimately rage quit the game which most likely eliminated my chance of buying the sequel. it is worth noting that the developers still seem to update this game, but it has been out for a 1.5 years and I encountered major problems that weren't fixed. I can much reccommend Torchlight II, Path of Exile, Titan Quest, Diablo II/III, Darkspore and potentiall Grim Dawn over this. I REALLY want to add TIAVH to that list of good ARPGs, but my experience was ruined and it comes at a difficult recommendation. If you are looking specifically for this type of gameplay, then play the other games I mentioned. If you are more interested in the Van Helsing universe and setting, then this and possibly the sequene are probably the best video games you will get based on the world.

Van Helsing is a good indie aRPG. I say indie, because if this had been released from a well known publisher it would have been treated as garbage and been on every 80% off sale it could find. Why do I say that? Well first let me just say that I wholly recommend this game! It's very fun and engaging. It presents a decent reward system. The graphics and sounds go along well with the pace of the action. So why call it garbage?
I didn't, I said it would have been treated as garbage had it been released from a big company. Van Helsing has bugs... Game breaking bugs wherein you can not complete main/storyline quests. Multiplayer bugs where games will just crash randomly or lag for no apparent reason or even spawn you into places where you are not supposed to reach thereby making you have to quit and return to the game. No tutorial for advanced features. Want to know how to upgrade (socket) items? So do I, go look for a youtube video, because this game honestly never tells you. The sounds, while going along well are somewhat repetative or campy. Also, the graphics, while they look well, enemies have a tendency to blend into the scene making it hard to know if you've killed everyone. It sports a strange control scheme and has no option to evade combat. If you're ranged and you get swarmed you can't run away because clicking in any direction means you're going to auto-attack. Also, if you have a controller plugged in, the game will not allow you to use a mouse and keyboard. You must exit, disconnect the controller, and restart the game.
Wooo... That was a long list of dislikes! I'm sorry, but I want you to know what you're getting into if you decide to purchase this title. Van Helsing has issues, BUT the game is fun! There is good dialogue and a story that makes sense. How many aRPG's have a story... and that makes sense!? The action is paced very well and never gets boring. There are quite a few quests to complete and I never had an issue figuring out where to go to complete them. Even though there are bugs the development team is working hard to correct them. Yes there are some instances where quests can't be completed, but until that's fixed, they've released a patch where you can bring up a console and complete the quest you're stuck on. The DLC classes provide more options. I like the Thaumaturge class. I'm very squishy, but I can take down the largest of monsters with ease.
So here's my final recommendation: If you like aRPG's and are looking for something to fill the gap between releases from big companies then I say grab this title. You will not be dissapointed. If aRPG's are not in your cup of tea, this game will not change your mind. If you are on the fence, just look over my comments about the bads and the goods. If you can live with the bads I think you'll find a lot of fun to be had here!

The aim of the game
Morak the magician created the gauntlet for power & got trapped inside. Your job is to fight through hordes or mummies, walking dead, undead, skeletons, grunts, orcs, etc., to bring him 3 shards of a sword so he can escape the gauntlet. In return he promises riches & power.
The Characters, their weapons & attacking skills
Thor (Warrior): Carries a battle axe and does large sweeping slashes which lay waste to the enemy. Can also do a double handed vertical chop (think log splitting). And when in a bind, a spinning attack which decimates the hordes around him. And can do a charge to barge the enemy out of the way.
Thyra (Valkyrie): Has a Shield, sword and speer. For close quarter combat she slashes with her sword. When the enemies are nearby she can throw her shield (Capt America style) and take out groups or lines of enemies. And she has a speer thrust which can also take out a line of enemy fast, as well as get her out of a swarming group. She also has a shield block which reflects projectiles back at the enemy who threw them at her and protects her from the slashes of sharp fingernailed attackers. She can move while she has the shield up, although slower.
Questor (Elf): He has a bow and arrow and an elf bomb which he can drop on the ground or attach to his snipe arrows. His normal arrows are rapid fire and short range. His snipe shot is longer range and has more power but isn't as rapid. Use the snipe/bomb arrow to shoot into a Summoning stone from afar - or single enemy troop and the troops around will blow up. His elf bomb can also be dropped into the middle of a horde to blow them up. For quick escapes he has a tumble roll.
Merlin (Wizard): He has 9 basic spells to choose from... Close quarter ice (freezes enemy in place), Ice beam (think laser beam) and Ice lob bomb (which creates a frozen circle which slows down the enemy. Fire balls (not as rapid as elf arrows but do more damage), fire lob bomb and can move quickly as a couple of snaking fireball things. Chain lightening, a force blast which knocks over the enemy and a force shield he and others can stand in.
Lillith (Necromancer): An add on character which can be purchased seperately to the game itself, her stock standard weapons are a small skeleton which rises to swipe the enemy a distance from her and a large skeleton with a sledge hammer that bashes down on groups of enemy or large items. As she takes out an enemy she gains some of their Soul Energy which she can use to raise a small group of fighters to help her.
Weapon Abilities
Each character can change their main weapon to give it slightly different abilities. E.g. choose a different bow and the elf's bomb becomes a "keep enemy in place" bomb and allows you to then kill them while they stand still. His normal arrows are not changed when this bow is used. The warrior can change his axe so that the double handed log splitting chop wipes out all the enemies around him in one blow. Valkyrie and Wiz also have different abilities.
Talismans
These change what happens when a potion is used. At the beginning the use of a potion simply blows it up and damages anything in the blast zone. Later they can be changed E.g. One use for the Valkyries becomes creating 3 valks to fight for her. Each character's Taslisman change is different.
Relics
Theses are items you can buy in the game (with gold earned in the game) to enhance your character's abilties. Some enable you to move faster, others create a whirlwind around you. One creates illusions of your character which can attack the enemy along side you.
Q&A - Answering unasked questions and bad review claims
Bad review claim: The game lacks content.
My take: Without any elaboration in what way it lacks content, the statement isn't helpful and says more about the reviewer than the game. The game has 30 missions in Campaign mode, which can be played on Easy, Normal or Hard, so it is kind of like 90 different missions. Each can be played with one of four main characters for a total possible 360 possible different mission experiences. Add to this the Endless option which has you go through an endless number of floors which are made up on the fly - and can be done solo or with others. The top players have reached floor 8,192!!! And then there is the Colleseum which pits you against waves of beasties in a one room arena - 6 waves completes the mission and each day there is a new mission with different gameplay in a new arena. I wouldn't call that "lack of content".
Bad review claim: Only 6 to 8 hrs of game play.
My take: At the time of this review I have over 140 hrs of game time. I only have 30 of 46 achievements, have not completed the campaign fully by myself in Normal or Hard mode in any single character. Have only managed to get to floor 79 in Endless mode with a team of people (only managed floor 8 by myself as elf) and have completed only two missions in the Colesseum. Makes me wonder if those who think "only 6 to 8 hours" actually tried or just rode along in easy mode multiplayer until the campaign was done and then called it quits, or just found the game too hard. Because with all the achievements, character upgrades and missions, there is no way it can all be done in only 6 to 8 hours.
Bad review claim: Boring.
Again, without elaboration the statement is meaninless. Boring compared to what? Would they find the classic games like Space Invaders or Pacman or Donkey Kong boring? Millions of people around the globe used to go out of their way to play those games in "pinball parlors". There is so much which can be done in this game, any claim it is boring, says more about the reviewer than the game itself.
I have a sneaky feeling the "lacks content", "only a few hours game play" and "boring" reviewers are most likely young kids. Maybe it's boring because their mates won't play with them, because maybe their mates think fps is the shiznits and everything else is boring? And I can see "kids" completing a room in easy mode and considerig it "done" without going back there ever in any other character or harder mode. Or the game is too hard for them so instead of admitting they find it too hard, blame the game for lack of content, not long in hours or boring.
Fact is, the graphics are good, the game play is progressively harder (something all good games have in common), it can be played in a mode that suits your skill level and is great for people who suffer video game motion sickness. It can be played on your own whenever you want to spend a few minutes playing, or played with friends or even strangers and can be played in a variety of characters.
You do not Need to play it in multiplayer. You can play it by yourself in single player mode without interacting with the server and other players. Most of my gameplay is like this as I use the time to get better with the various characters (so I'll be a good asset to any multiplayer team I join) and when I don't have the time to complete the campaign or whatnot with others and want to spend 15 or 30 minutes playing, or just don't feel like playing with others. Playing solo means you can go at your own pace and fully explore each mission in the campaign.
Sometimes, depending on the time of day, finding a stranger to play Campaign is difficult. But if you head into Endless more you will Always find someone in there to play with.

It is a shame, this game has potential and I have been following since the beginning.  But then, poor choices started being made in my opinion.  The premise, and how the game originally was, started out was great!  You are in a remote cold wilderness with only your village, that is awesome and it seemed believable. But update after update I started to see the negative pop in.  With that said, this game has many positives that I will explain below.  Don't let these negatives scare you off, because you might love what I dislike. This review will change as the game cahnges.
NEGATIVES
To start, what is with this ridiculous alien looking stuff scattered around the map?  What started out as a humble game in an Alaskan or Canadian wilderness, turned into a strange, almost foreign wilderness that isn't believable anymore.
The second major update got rid of the wonderful first map the game had and turned it into strange islands connected by snow drifts . . . it was as dumb as it sounds.
I loved this game in it's earliest stages with the first map that had small towns scattered around, and places to explore.  It was more realistic, and not this goofy fantasy world it is now. I hate to see something that had so much promise go so far the wrong way.
POSITIVES
What this game does right is many things.  The music is relaxing and wonderful.  The scenery and nature is simplistic, but at times you do feel lost out there as the stars loom over your head.  The graphics continue to get better and the sense of place, and atmosphere is there.  They have done a wonderful job at capturing this (it just gets ruined when you find an alien beacon, or weirdly shaped rocks that look unnatural).
The sense of calm yet, inside urgency to get supplies before the next storm is always there.  Sometimes it is hard to feel that urgency with the peaceful music, but when you realize your village depends on you to get supplies before the storm, you feel that pressure.
Simple customization of your dogs was a nice touch.
This game does something in a really cool setting, and I hope they can stay on track with that focus.
CONCLUSION
I am sure the creators have great intentions, and they have improved many things such as game mechanics, and graphics, but it is quickly turning into a game I don't care for anymore due to some poor choices.  This isn't the original game I supported, and that is really unfortunate.  I wish I could give this game a mixed review, but I can't.  This game does many things right, but the few things it does wrong are so jarringly out there, it will have you scratching your head.

Impressive for something still in alpha and still fixing things.
If you're looking to get lost in the snow for a while, consider Eternal Winter. It's not as evil as Don't Starve, but when it comes to survival, these games are probably cousins in the same "Haha, You Suck! Now You're Going to Die Because You're Inept!" Survival Games. The graphics are fairly simple and yet the snowy landscape is just beautiful to look at. You're not alone out there with your village and it's a competition for survival. It only makes that beautiful night sky that much more depressing.
You're given weapons, a sled team (DOGGIES!), some basic resources, and some buddies so you can all hopefully not die together. Your pals at your village have some basic advice which you'll hopefully heed...or you can go run off into the wilderness with just your long underwear.
This game really doesn't give you much instruction on how to do anything. There's no tutorial level. There are helpful reminders on what E does in each screen, but otherwise you're on your own on what button does what. Good thing is that you've probably used these buttons dozens of times in other games and they still do similar in this game. It's a minor annoyance that there's absolutely nothing there, but you'll get over it.
Finding food can also be absolutely terrible and daunting. That's why I've paused. I'm afraid to go back to hunt for food right now. There are animals out there that want to eat me and my puppies. Yikes. I also failed to track a deer. Otherwise there was absolutely no food to find. Listen I get we're in some snowy wasteland but that was really difficult and frustrating.
I'm also a total waste at shooting the gun. At least I have other weapons, but really? Thankfully I can avoid combat with other humans for the most part, but I really need food here. This is another minor annoyance and I'm sure I'll get better at it with time.
The worst I've found is that it's a bit buggy. The graphics vanished at one point and I was left with this strange orange wasteland I walked around until I decided to start a new game. Such is the problem with alpha, but it seems like bugs get ironed out fairly quickly so I'm not too worried about that.
Truthfully, there's something appealing to building your own village of wasteland dwellers and trying to survive in the cold. I have a bias towards town building and managing their needs. With a giant map to explore and things to scavenge, this seems like a sure thing and I'm optimistic about the future of this game.
There's nothing worrying for a health warning so far. No blinking lights. No disco rave. You've got stars dotting the sky and a warm fire's glow. Those two things are worth mentioning just in case, but I don't think that'll spark your migraine or light sensitivity unless you're incredibly sensitive. But uh, you know. This is a video game. Act with caution when you game.

If you haven't played The New Order yet, I suggest waiting to play this. But don't worry about The Old Blood - it is a good game, but it doesn't add enough story that you'd have to play it to understand the New Colossus.
Story is excellent so far. It picks up immediately where the New Order left off. Right when you begin, B.J. will have a flashback of the events of the New Order, including the beginning where you're forced to decide if you want to save Fergus or Wyatt. But this time, it has a pretty major impact on the story. Additionally, you'll have a different weapon for each time line. Fergus gives you a remodled LaserKraftWerk, while Wyatt gives you the DieselKraftWork (as in diesel gas, not Vin Disel). I'm not going to spoil any of the story though, so I'll cut it off there. However, keep in mind this game may be very offensive to some people. You will hear the usage of the "N-word," nazis are referred to as "fascist pigs" (I dunno, apparently fascism is a sensitive topic), there are KKK members in addition to Nazis, etc. But what do you expect, this takes place in the 1960's - and this is a depiction of if the Nazis won WWII.
There are many improvements to the gameplay. Remember how in the New Order, you can drop an armored soldier like a fly with a single head shot from the silenced pistol, even from a mile away? Not anymore. Even using the Sturmgewehr (long-range rifle) with a scope won't kill a soldier with a head shot if there's a large distance between. Enemies will also respond do dead bodies, looking around the area. Even shooting silenced bullets generates enough sound to distract nearby enemies. Throughout the game, you'll find weapon upgrade kits. These allow you to upgrade any weapon, each has about 3 upgrades. You'll get upgrades like silencers, scopes, drum mags/extended clips, high-powered bullets, etc. Ammo/health/armor pick-up is similar to RtCW: sometimes, you'll automatically pick these items up, but other times, you'll have to press the use button. So if you're trying to save ammo for later, don't run over it just to be safe.
You still get perks, but I personally thing they downgraded the system. Instead of performing a task for a perk, then unlocking the next, you just do the same thing over and over again to level up each perk. Example: preform X amount of headshots for this perk, then when you're done with that, perform even more headshots to level this perk up more. Perk progress still saves regardless of making it to the next checkpoint, so if you're like me and started out on a higher difficulty, you may die often, and end up maxing out a perk early in the game.
There's a crap ton of collectibles (over 300, several different types of collectibles). When you kill one of the Officers (forgot what they called those ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s), they drop an enigma code. Rather than only being a certain amount of Enigma Codes, there's an unlimited amount of them, and they will be used later in the game for what's basically a Bounty Board. So you'll definitely want to collect those.
The graphics are frikin' stunning. But to Hell with the graphics - you're not just a pair of floating arms with a gun, when you look down, you actually see your legs and body! I know that even with the technology of today, that's almost impossible (I mean, why else do you think that feature is in very few FPS games?). The game runs smoother as♥♥♥♥♥♥ too. I've had very few crashes (one, maybe two), but I guess it's common to have crashing issues and other issues. However, there is one thing almost every player experiences: whenever they release a new patch, the game just crashes upon starting up, or the patch causes major lag. Manually downloading the latest driver from the manufacturer's site usually solves the issue, but still annoying nevertheless.
Oh, and you get to play Wolfenstein 3D in it's entirety (including the Nocturnal Missions). In the base, you'll come across an arcade machine, called "Wolfstone 3D." The levels are the same as the classic, but you'll notice that you're playing as a Nazi and killing resistance members. So instead of Swastikas and portraits of Hitler, you'll see Kreisau Circle logos and portraits of Blazko. Awesome and funny little nod to the classic game.

If you like 2D Fighters like Street Fighter or Tekken you will love Skullgirls.

Skullgirls is a classic styled 2D fighting game, in the vein of Street Fighter, Guilty Gear and my personal favourite BlazBlue series, created by Lab Zero Games and published by Autumn Games and Marvelous AQL.
Gameplay:
Skullgirls works like an classic six-button arcade fighting game, but with a unique tag-battle system, which can pit different teams of one, two or three against one another
The controls feel fluid and the anti-infinite combo system, works great in preventing spammable exploits.
*Bonus*
The final boss of the story mode will be cheap as all hell to beginners.
Graphics:
This is the area where Skullgirls' artist Alex Ahad's skill shines, Every character is hand-drawn in high-resolution and with amazing smoothness in animation, this paired with beautiful 3D stage backgrounds akin to BlazBlue, makes the game look gorgeous during tense fights with lots of flashy special moves.
*Bonus*
The character designs for the female characters, may cause arousal in prebpubescent males
Story:
Skullgirls has a great but a little bit confusing storyline, which is placed into little snippets and pieces throughout the game's Story mode and is expanded upon in the DLC characters' Story modes
Music and Sounds:
This game's Soundtrack is amazing and memorable and features tracks written by Michiru Yamane (Suikoden and Castlevania), Vincent Diamante (Flower) Blaine McGurty and Brenton Kossak
Overall:
The game is one of the best fighting games made in a long while, has great art and music, and is also really cheap for what it's worth the game is also available on: PS3, XBOX360 with Encore 2 being released for PS4 and PSVita

This game is a lot of things. A feels trip is just one of them.
Like any Otome or Visual Novel, the plot and characters are the backbone making up Nameless, and Cheritz has executed them very well. The characters in particular are all lovable and/or sympathetic, some more than others (but that is usually up to the player's own personal preference). That being said, I'd like to give a small round of applause for Cheritz' brilliant move of having a character from Dandelion (one of their other Otome games), be integral to Nameless' plot. The MC, Eri, is also quite relatable. She's quirky, sassy and down to earth, making for some hilarious moments.
The art and music are very soothing to look at and listen to, with purplish hues and tones adding to the atmosphere. The graphics and interface are great, and the localization is also well done, with proper English grammar and spelling mostly consistent throughout the game. The plot itself is intriguing and mysteriously sinister, with dark themes scattered throughout. Don't expect this to be a light-hearted read; interacting with the boys and learning about the true plot behind the scenes, you may very well end up shedding a tear or two.

It's fun for most of the campaign, but only so-so as typing practice if you can already touch-type. Typing is mostly focused on random words, which is not really the same as typing sentences. For random words I can do about 60wpm. For sentences I can do about 90wpm.
The setting is interesting, somewhat like Bastion in the way the landscape unfolds, but with a distinct style.
Movement is a little awkward. I kept hitting corners. I found it easier to use WASD than the recommended EFIJ. I wish it supported IJKL movement.
I think it was a mistake to start the character with slow movement and make faster movement an upgrade, since the slowness has no effect on combat and just makes exploring more tedious.
The various button puzzles are cute and mostly easy, except for times when I struggled with getting movement right.
The 4 different spells are interesting but tended to mess up my typing.
Ice just slows enemies. It's the most straightforward. I'm still typing every word I see.
Fire destroys an additional word on the same enemy in a slow but predictable way, so it's pretty easy to just switch among available enemies while Fire takes effect.
Spark destroys additional words on other enemies in an unpredictable way. This is annoying, but often the most powerful and useful, since typing a short word can also destroy several long words. I ended up using this most of the time in the defense waves.
Wind pushes back enemies, which often pushes them offscreen, making their words unavailable until they come back. This power sucks. The unpredictability of the sudden unavailability of words messes up my typing rhythm. I think the idea was for Wind to be helpful when there are crowds of enemies, since typing one word can push back the group. But in practice, Spark is  more effective on groups and requires less typing.
Switching between spells is kind of annoying, but fortunately there are only a few waves where switching is necessary, and the sequence of enemy types is always the same, so it's easy to learn a particular sequence of attack/switch.

To the Moon is an RPG-like game in which you play two employees of Sigmund Corp., a company that is hired to change people's memories in order to fullfil their dying wishes. Dr. Watts and Dr. Rosalene, are, thus, contacted to fullfil an old man's (Johnny) wish of going to the moon. For that, they backtrack through his memories, starting at his most recent one, until they reach a point where they can inject his will to become an astronaut, leaving his own mind to fill the gaps after that. At each memory, they must find a memento, an object that will link back to an older memory upon activation.
As the player plays through the memories, a beautiful, and sometimes painful, story unfolds.
This game is
a technical gem. The mechanics are simple enough, and it looks like a project a beginner game designer could make on Engine 001. Sometimes, some things felt awkward (for me at least), specially with the change of the cursos icon, and the characters movement (choosing weird routes when point-and-clicking, and not doing as predicted when using a controler).
The switch from regular RPG to a puzzle during the preparation of the mementos is something that I quite enjoyed.
If this game is not a technical gem, I'd easily say it is an artistic one.
Although the graphics are very simple, and mostly "uneventfull", there are one or two moments where even they shine.
But the graphics are far from what makes this game an artistic gem. It's story and music make it so.
The story is sometimes beautiful, sometimes painful, sometimes hauting. The story of two lovers
. At each memory we get a new look at things, and in my opinion it beautifully brought to light a desease (
) through a couple of characters with different struggles, and stories. It is a game that quite possibly will have you cry, as well as laugh at the ever so inadequate jokes of Dr. Neil Watt. (Who, it should be noted, seems to be a fan of How I Met Your Mother and Doctor Who).
Finally, the music.
The music of this game is absolutely beautiful in it's simplicity yet emotion. It shows how it can create ambiance, from mre cheerful moments, to sadder tones, to mysterious, even a bit suspenseful. If the story alone won't make you feel, put a good headset on and you're either gonna cry, or gonna have your eyes begin to tear up, or you're just not human.
I absolutely recommend this game. It's a great, simple piece that shows us that videogames are, truly, a form of art (it actually will literally tell you that on one of the DLC's, like that was needed)
P.S.: I've played the first DLC (the holliday special miniepisode), but not yet the seccond. It is also a beautiful piece at different moments, and for different reasons. I do feel, however, that a chance was wasted at telling other stories, and from other points of view. However, the universe was expanded in a new and interesting way.
P.P.S.: Though this game reminded me of
, I sill felt at moments that I would like to watch a movie of it, were it well made. And by well made I mean take one of the tangents that the game offers, instead of telling the same story. Perhaps one of Dr.s Watt and Rosalene's old cases, perhaps someone one of someone else's from Sigmund Corp.

Van Helsing is a fun 20 hour campaign. The story is interesting and the strained relationship between Van Helsing and his ghost companion makes for some often funny dialogue.  The music is excellent, the mouse & keyboard controls work well and the animation is well done.  The only gripe I have is the replay value is somewhat limiting since you're tied to a melee or a ranged character.  Buying one of the two optional DLC characters helps fill out the game with more skills.
For people like me who like to explore and clear out maps, there are tons of treasure chests sprinkled everywhere.  Plus there are special "trophy" monsters to fight which give you an achievement and extra loot. Finally, you can continue a completed campaign in what is called "Never Ending Story" mode with increasingly difficult monsters.  Characters over level 30 can be imported into the sequel.
I think Van Helsing is an underrated gem and I recommended it to Torchlight fans and action RPG fans in general.  Don't take my word for it, though.  Neocore Games released a playable demo so you can try it out for yourself.

Gauntlet Slayer edition is a fairly enjoyable update of the ancient arcade game. The basic premise is that you have to fight your way through various dungeons , in either single player or co-op, gathering up coins and food. Coins can be spent on upgrades, whereas food replenishes your health. One of the games little twists , however, is that trigger happy players can accidentally destroy the food, or potions that act like smartbombs, if they're not careful.
It's one of a few systems that alleviates somewhat repetitive gameplay mechanics. There are objects that constantly spawn monsters until destroyed, and it can mean the players faces wave after wave of enemies, unless they target these objects. It's both a source of excitement: as you desperately try to staunch the flow, and also partly why the game gets tedious - as it happens in almost every room.
The upgrades system adds a little variety, and they do all have a pronounced effect on how each character plays, but you can only have three at once. So it doesn't really shake up the gameplay all that drastically. The dev's have tried some things to mix up the action - one nice touch is that some levels have an unbeatable enemy who phazes in and out of existence, meaning the player is trying to thin out the hordes while dodging the other baddie when it appears (as it's touch is instant death).
It also has some boss battles which use either the environment, or more dynamic attacks than the standard enemies. It certainly has much more depth than the original, but it's best enjoyed in small doses - though thankfully most of the levels aren't huge anyway.
It's reasonable entertainment in single player, and I would expect it's rather good fun in co-op, as there is a competitive side to that: food and gold isn't shared between players, and in the heat of the moment stray attacks could pulverize food / potions. It would also deal with the games biggest problem (beyond it being repetitive) which is: it's too easy on normal difficulty, yet frustratingly hard on the hard difficulty. A second player would help there.
Overall it's not bad - a fun game in modest doses, in co-op it's probably much more enjoyable. It looks nice enough, sounds quite reasonable, and plays pretty well - at least with the understanding it's not Diablo 3, and was always a budget title.

Let me clarify the thumbs down.  This game gets thumbs down because it is not Gauntlet, I will elaborate.  The game is a decent hack n slash party game with a fun challenge, but calling it Gauntlet is a lie and is deceiving to fans.
I was excited as ♥♥♥♥ to see this game's trailer, they made it look so pretty and fast paced and fun, bringing back that Nintendo64 gauntlet adventure feeling.  Turning that old game on was always like being transported to another gigantic epic adventure with all the unique levels, bosses, tons of items along the way for weapon mutations or familiars that join you.  Not to mention items that unlock secret levels or characters, lots of interesting and fun cutscenes, and a wide variety of puzzles to interact with unique to each world.
THIS GAME trades all of that for pretty colours and getting to change your helmet, weapon, a cape, and alternating what potions do, and some spells.  This basically negates all of the fun of what Gauntlet was.  Your primary focus has now become taking all the gold, which just makes people mad, because without gold, you cannot buy weapons.  You are also correct in realizing that no weapons/item purchases mean no variance in your gameplay.  All ability and weapon and spell augmentations are tied to weapons or tomes you purchase in the store.  Note that not even all of the store items even do anything, most are purely cosmetic.
I mean so yeah, having a unique inventory to your character is cool, and buying your own special♥♥♥♥♥♥is nice, but…at the cost of what?  Well you judge that.
Other things that take away from the game are the fact that you cannot kill death anymore, at least it's more obscure than it was in the original games.  Why does using a potion not kill death?  Was this some dumb unlockable ability for one hero that he has to buy in the store to be able to do?  Before, any character could use a potion to dispel death.  Now they have turned levels in which he exclusively appears (no more opening a chest for treasure, no death popping out of a chest!) he is turned into basically an outrun the lava level.  It's not timed, but he really enforces you to proceed quite quickly due to following you quickly and being huge.
There are no more worlds, it's a straight shot down, barely any change up of enemy diversity, I felt like I was fighting the same monster the entire game, and there were very few bosses, nothing was themed or engaging.  Grind grind, get gold, buy shitx666
Whoo.  So, maybe I didn't play this enough?  Is there more to this game?  Does it open up into everything I am criticizing it for missing?  Maybe so, and if so then that's too bad.  I invested around 8 good hours with 3-4 fluctuating people involved and it was of the consistent content I have previously described.  So if there is more, then frankly that's a damn shame that it would take so long to getting back to a game so timelessly classic as Gauntlet.  I understand Gauntlet changed through generations and Midway no longer exists, so clearly the same heart was not in the production of this game.  I'm not interested in investing that much time in a game that is nothing what I was told it was.  They used key factors reminiscent of the old game to draw you in and cheated people out of how many dollars is this game?  15? 25? 30?  I don't know right now, but whatever the price, it's not worth more than 5$ if you call it Gauntlet.  Yeah sure you put the music from the old games in, there was a wizard, you shot the food, and you said "Red wizard needs food badly", but come on, that doesn't make a game.
Like I said, it was a decent party game, and it was enjoyable.  I just spent the entire time trying to be entertained like I was with Dark Legacy or Legends, but it never happened.  It's like they didn't even try.

Assassin's Creed Chronicles is essentially what I would picture if someone took all the developers from the original prince of Persia games, and told them to go make me an Assassin Chronicles game. It's also my favourite entry in the 'Chronicles' series for assassin creed.
Gameplay wise, Chronicles is 2.5D, meaning- whilst you can run and jump about the stage, you also have the ability to slip onto different lanes in the game, which provides an interesting nuance to navigating about the area via platforming, climbing, and what have you. Moreover, whilst you -are- more than capable of getting through the game in one giant hectic Murder-a-thon, it rewards you for being subtle in your approach - as being unseen (and a pacifist) provides you with the largest amount of points, and points are used to unlock upgrades to your character.
As the game progresses, you'll gradually gain a decent array of (upgradeable) item and abilities to bypass opponents and obstacles- allowing situations to be approached in a more open ended fashion. Which makes the newgame + mode a bit more entertaining to romp through.
As for the story. It's a fairly basic revenge plot set within the universe of Assassin's Creed mythology.

If you haven't played The New Order yet, I suggest waiting to play this. But don't worry about The Old Blood - it is a good game, but it doesn't add enough story that you'd have to play it to understand the New Colossus.
Story is excellent so far. It picks up immediately where the New Order left off. Right when you begin, B.J. will have a flashback of the events of the New Order, including the beginning where you're forced to decide if you want to save Fergus or Wyatt. But this time, it has a pretty major impact on the story. Additionally, you'll have a different weapon for each time line. Fergus gives you a remodled LaserKraftWerk, while Wyatt gives you the DieselKraftWork (as in diesel gas, not Vin Disel). I'm not going to spoil any of the story though, so I'll cut it off there. However, keep in mind this game may be very offensive to some people. You will hear the usage of the "N-word," nazis are referred to as "fascist pigs" (I dunno, apparently fascism is a sensitive topic), there are KKK members in addition to Nazis, etc. But what do you expect, this takes place in the 1960's - and this is a depiction of if the Nazis won WWII.
There are many improvements to the gameplay. Remember how in the New Order, you can drop an armored soldier like a fly with a single head shot from the silenced pistol, even from a mile away? Not anymore. Even using the Sturmgewehr (long-range rifle) with a scope won't kill a soldier with a head shot if there's a large distance between. Enemies will also respond do dead bodies, looking around the area. Even shooting silenced bullets generates enough sound to distract nearby enemies. Throughout the game, you'll find weapon upgrade kits. These allow you to upgrade any weapon, each has about 3 upgrades. You'll get upgrades like silencers, scopes, drum mags/extended clips, high-powered bullets, etc. Ammo/health/armor pick-up is similar to RtCW: sometimes, you'll automatically pick these items up, but other times, you'll have to press the use button. So if you're trying to save ammo for later, don't run over it just to be safe.
You still get perks, but I personally thing they downgraded the system. Instead of performing a task for a perk, then unlocking the next, you just do the same thing over and over again to level up each perk. Example: preform X amount of headshots for this perk, then when you're done with that, perform even more headshots to level this perk up more. Perk progress still saves regardless of making it to the next checkpoint, so if you're like me and started out on a higher difficulty, you may die often, and end up maxing out a perk early in the game.
There's a crap ton of collectibles (over 300, several different types of collectibles). When you kill one of the Officers (forgot what they called those ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s), they drop an enigma code. Rather than only being a certain amount of Enigma Codes, there's an unlimited amount of them, and they will be used later in the game for what's basically a Bounty Board. So you'll definitely want to collect those.
The graphics are frikin' stunning. But to Hell with the graphics - you're not just a pair of floating arms with a gun, when you look down, you actually see your legs and body! I know that even with the technology of today, that's almost impossible (I mean, why else do you think that feature is in very few FPS games?). The game runs smoother as♥♥♥♥♥♥ too. I've had very few crashes (one, maybe two), but I guess it's common to have crashing issues and other issues. However, there is one thing almost every player experiences: whenever they release a new patch, the game just crashes upon starting up, or the patch causes major lag. Manually downloading the latest driver from the manufacturer's site usually solves the issue, but still annoying nevertheless.
Oh, and you get to play Wolfenstein 3D in it's entirety (including the Nocturnal Missions). In the base, you'll come across an arcade machine, called "Wolfstone 3D." The levels are the same as the classic, but you'll notice that you're playing as a Nazi and killing resistance members. So instead of Swastikas and portraits of Hitler, you'll see Kreisau Circle logos and portraits of Blazko. Awesome and funny little nod to the classic game.

My first review!

Artwork: 9/10
So I played through the game like normal, from Lance to the 'first doll you received'. First things first though. Lemme just squeel on the beautiful artwork. I mean, how could you not!? I'm talking about BEAUTIFUL. I'd rush to the nearest store if I ever find out they are selling Nameless posters and wallpaper. So there you go, superbly beautiful artwork.
Story: 3.5/10
Well, about this part, I have to say that it was kind of a let down. For almost half of the time, I think I nearly slept through some of the characters path (I'm looking at you, Red and Yeon Ho). And the main character's awfully bland personality didn't help spice up the story either. I mean sure, you got beautiful drawn characters and CG, but at the end of the day, its the story that counts. Look at Higurashi, Umineko and erm, Touhou? They both had crap artwork, but at the very least, story was fascinating enough for people to overlook that 'art'.
Soundtrack: 6/10
The soundtrack was comforting and relaxing, too bad the music is not my kind of taste. Still, I know beautiful music when I hear one, so hats off to Shinjou Hanabi for creating music that matched the game's atmosphere and 'school' theme.
Character: 5/10
I wasn't expecting much the moment I saw the female MC. At that instant I knew she is definitely going to be bland. Boy I was right. Not to mention she was SUPER DUPER dense. Holy Jesus and blessed Mary. I can't count the number of times I was screaming at the screen yelling "WHAT IS WRONG WITH YOU SENPAI NOTICED YOU STOP PLAYING DUMB". Being dense makes the situation hilarious, but TOO dense is the ultimate (okay, maybe not ultimate, but close enough) recipe for character disaster. Its a huge relieft to find out at least the boys have unique personalities from kuu-tsundere clingy playboy yandere naive yangire (I think?). Gotta admit that even Soi's dramatic comments made me laugh more than the boys did. Seriously, that's even the reason why the ratings are like bare-minimum pass.
Translation: 8/10
I've certainly seen better translated games in my life, but that's not to say Nameless isn't good. In fact I think they did a good job translating it, with a few minor hiccups here and there which can easily be overlooked since its mainly grammar problems. Language is easy to grasp so I doubt anyone would have even a single problem understanding any of the scripts.
Overall: 6/10
Since its only my opinion and I'm a little extremely biased AGAINST bland female MC, so there might be prejudice here and there. However, if you don't mind the female MC being of plain character, then you might enjoy the game more than I did. Hopefully.

I have a played a lot of otome games (otoge). I must say that thus far, this is the best one in terms of character development, individual character stories, and overarching plot. Each playthrough of a route gives the game a different feeling while still reminding you of the overall undertone. One tip that I must mention is that after you finish a character, start a new game. I am one of those people who usually start from where the common route branches (because I keep a save from that point), but you will experience the story more fully if you play from the start again; even if you have to skip the already read text.
Also, a big recommendation would be to play the characters in the suggested route order (and of course to play all the characters). The order is as follows: Lance, Yeonho, Yuri, Tei, and then Red. It is already suggested in the way that the routes are locked anyway, but I highly recommend it.
Nameless is really fantastic! I would say that the game is near perfect. The reason I say ‘near’ is because the downfall to Nameless is its translation/proofreading. As I played, I saw quite a few typos or slight grammatical errors. It’s a bit disappointing to see that they had people proofread the translations but they had still missed so many errors. It’s a bit distracting, but overall, I would say that it doesn’t take away from the story at all.
All in all, I would say that if you are a otoge fan (or are interested in it), this is a must-read. This may become my go-to otoge to recommend when people are interested in getting into the genre.

Summary:
Extremely strong cinematic experience, but lacking in actual gameplay for price.
Would recommend purchace on sale (for under 10.00GBP / 12.98USD) or watching a silent playthrough on youtube.
Firstly, I do not dislike the game at all. It's beautifully rendered, the atmosphere is fantastic, the storytelling and mythological aspects are on point. The whispers / madness mechanic is very well done (although gets annoying towards the end, especially when it starts talking over a rune story to tell me something obvious), and adds character and atmosphere to the game in SPADES.
The animation, texturing and terrain is all exceptionally well done (aside from a single time my sword decided to stick to my face). Occasionally slips into the uncanny valley on the facials, but is generally prety good.
The combat engine is perfectly decent. Whilst simple in its mechanics, it is fluid and gets the job done with no bother. It is by no means hard, however - with the exception of an insta-kill attack in the midgame and another in the final boss, I didn't die in combat at all.
A few annoying instances of narrative breaking mecanics - such as dropping a thing we had previously held secure through hell and high water for no reason whatsoever. Protagonist making clearly questonable decisions (obvious trap etc) but providing no alternative for the aware gamer simply because the story demanded it.
However, it was 24.99GBP / 32.44USD. For a 7 hour game, this is already quite a lot. For a game that is at least half cutscene and cinematic wandering, this is too much.
For the same price you could get any number of games that would keep you actually playing for much much longer. This is an excellent rendering tech demo. A masterclass in cinematics
and atmosphere. A top notch representation of mental health, associated stigmatism and effects of childhood trauma. But as a game? Not enough for the price.
